### [accent-picker](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/accent-picker)

[★ 314](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/stargazers "314 GitHub stars")

OKLCH accent colour picker for the Hermes Desktop status bar: drag it and the whole theme retints live, with palette commands to reset to the theme default or copy the current colour. A theme-authoring tool; the colour is scratch state and is never persisted. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface); no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

✓ Officialv1.0.0Desktop

### [quota](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/quota)

[★ 88](https://github.com/rarf/hermes-quota-plugin/stargazers "88 GitHub stars")

Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota\_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint using the hermes-quota-plugin User-Agent; optional additional Claude accounts read access tokens only from explicitly configured Claude Code credentials files and send them only to Anthropic's fixed OAuth usage endpoint (read-only, no refresh-token exchange or credential write-back; tokens and paths excluded from the quota cache). Linux extra accounts verified; Windows experimental, extra macOS Keychain accounts unsupported. The openai-codex check reads every saved Codex account from Hermes' own auth.json credential pool (read-only, never refreshed; expired accounts show reauth-required) and queries the Codex usage endpoint with the codex-cli User-Agent; the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json, Hermes' auth.json pool and OPENCODE\_GO\_API\_KEY\_N variables (read-only). The cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check reads local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux or the macOS Keychain for the browser's Safe Storage key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or Hermes' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek, openrouter, ollama (which may read OLLAMA\_API\_KEY from ~/.hermes/.env and calls ollama.com/api/usage and /api/me) and experientiallabs send keys from Hermes' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints.

❖ Communityv2.10.0Desktop2 hooks

### [hermes-resetwatch](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-resetwatch)

[★ 82](https://github.com/Adolanium/hermes-resetwatch/stargazers "82 GitHub stars")

Track subscription quotas and reset times in Hermes Desktop. Disclosure — probe.py re-executes itself under the Hermes Python interpreter located via HERMES\_PYTHON / VIRTUAL\_ENV / the parent process or the Hermes installer's managed venv (HERMES\_HOME/installs); it reads provider API keys from the Hermes .env, Hermes's own saved OAuth logins (auth.json credential pool, read-only), the Vaultwarden plugin's local secret cache (cache/vaultwarden\_cache.json, read-only, only when Vaultwarden is the sole enabled secret source) and Docker s6 container env files, plus other coding-assistant CLIs' local logins (including macOS keychain entries), and sends each key only to its own vendor's usage endpoint.

### [hermes-memory-ui](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-memory-ui)

[★ 74](https://github.com/xraysight/hermes-memory-ui/stargazers "74 GitHub stars")

Read-only Hermes Dashboard and Desktop plugin for inspecting built-in, holographic, Mem0, Honcho, Mnemosyne, Hindsight, and ByteRover memory. Disclosure — reads the active profile's memory files, provider configs and provider API keys (keys are never returned to the UI), and on user action sends search/recall/reflect queries with configured bank/peer/user IDs to the configured Mem0, Honcho and Hindsight endpoints (Hindsight Cloud default api.hindsight.vectorize.io) using those keys; ByteRover queries run the local \`brv\` CLI; for a local embedded Hindsight setup a contents read may start the \`hindsight-embed\` daemon; no memory is written.

[★ 13](https://github.com/outpoints/hermes-honcho-plugin/stargazers "13 GitHub stars")

Desktop workbench for the Honcho memory behind the focused chat: read the newest conclusions, trace their premises, search messages, ask scoped questions, and add confirmed corrections or source files. Uses each profile's existing Honcho provider configuration. Disclosure — talks only to the Honcho server each profile is already configured for, through Hermes's own Honcho client and credentials, and polls it about every 10 seconds for the focused chat while Desktop is open. Ask runs a Honcho reasoning call that may use credits. Add fact/correction and Add to session write to Honcho only after you confirm the target in a dialog; Add to session uploads the text or PDF/JSON/text file you choose. A chat from another local profile is read with that profile's own Honcho configuration, only where this plugin is enabled. It reads the focused chat's title and folder from the profile's session database, read-only. No telemetry.

A live board your agent builds for you: tabs of notes, tables, charts, KPI cards and live Hermes data, in the dashboard and Hermes Desktop. It appears as a Board tab in the dashboard and a page in Desktop, and the agent lays it out with 19 native boardstate\_\* tools, approval widgets included. Runs a local Node >= 20 sidecar on loopback with a per-spawn nonce; no network access unless you opt in to operator-gated connectors. Disclosure — spawns a local Node.js ≥20 sidecar (from PATH/HERMES\_NODE\_BIN, nothing downloaded) on 127.0.0.1 on first use; state under HERMES\_HOME/boardstate-state/. Reads the dashboard's loopback session token from Hermes internals (web\_server.\_SESSION\_TOKEN) and passes it to the sidecar for live usage/sessions/cron widgets; mounts one token-gated static route for approved widget assets. No outbound network unless you author boardstate.connectors.json (stdio/HTTP MCP connectors); connector actions need operator approval. Ships one plugin skill, boardstate:boardstate-report-problem, which drafts a bug report and files it with the GitHub CLI only after the user approves the exact text.

### [kanban-gantt](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/kanban-gantt)

[★ 10](https://github.com/e-is/hermes-kanban-gantt/stargazers "10 GitHub stars")

Gantt timeline view for the Hermes kanban boards: a full /kanban-gantt desktop page rendering any board as a timeline of real work timestamps (created/started/review/done), with a collapsible tree column (boxed fold controls, tree connectors, per-board fold state, multi-parent links kept visible), an optional List view beside the timeline (task, assignee, status, last activity — the timeline stays the default), task creation (project, workspace, skills, model override, goal mode), re-parenting by drag & drop or from the drawer, live-activity arcs, filters, bulk actions, and a dockable task detail drawer. Any task with files carries a paperclip: the file list is fetched on demand (the board payload carries a count per task), and each file gets a type-aware preview (markdown, plain text, image, PDF, HTML in a sandboxed frame) or a download. A period selector (6 h to 7 d) puts a slice of the timeline on screen in one click. Zero API keys, zero model tokens; live updates follow the plugin's /events websocket, which a gateway turns off with KANBAN\_GANTT\_WS=0 (the page then polls every 60 s and shows a Refresh button). Disclosure — Desktop page plus dashboard routes that read and write the local kanban boards (create tasks with workspace path, skills, model override and goal mode; re-parent; move a task, with its children, to another board — the copy is verified there before the source rows and their links are deleted; edit status, assignee and description; bulk archive and delete; read task attachment files from the board's own attachments folder for preview and download); live updates over a dashboard-authenticated /events websocket, off with KANBAN\_GANTT\_WS=0; no third-party network.

### [orbit-desktop](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/orbit-desktop)

[★ 7](https://github.com/mojomast/orbitdesktop/stargazers "7 GitHub stars")

Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Hermes. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit\_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime\_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research.

### [hermes-cloud-file-manager](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-cloud-file-manager)

[★ 4](https://github.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/stargazers "4 GitHub stars")

Cloud Files for Hermes Desktop — browse, search, create folders and bulk-upload files and whole folders to the machine your agent runs on, read and edit its Markdown and text files (view first; nothing is written until you review the line diff and press Save), import files from the agent's own Google Drive, and hand the agent file locations from the chat + menu without re-uploading. Built for remote gateways (token or sign-in); works locally too. Disclosure — adds a file API to the gateway (dashboard plugin routes under the gateway's existing auth) over the agent's working folders, by default terminal.cwd or else the gateway user's home with its dot-entries hidden. It lists and searches those folders, reads Markdown and text files, creates folders and writes uploads and Drive imports (staged as hidden .cfm-\* temp files in the destination folder; a name clash keeps both files). It overwrites only an existing .md/.markdown/.txt file you open and explicitly Save in its editor (refused if the file changed since you opened it). It never deletes your files (it removes only its own stale or aborted .cfm-\* temp files and staging folders), never follows links out of those folders, and never lists, reads or writes the agent's Hermes home apart from a working folder set inside it (roots, terminal.cwd, or a workspace/ folder it creates when the working folder would be the home itself). Its only network use is Google Drive, read-only, through the agent's own google-workspace skill, whose scripts (from skills/productivity/google-workspace in the agent's Hermes home, else the copy bundled with Hermes) it runs with the gateway's Python and a minimal environment without API keys; the plugin never reads the Google token. While Desktop is open it re-checks Drive sign-in about once a minute; otherwise it makes no network calls.

### [hermes-monitor](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-monitor)

[★ 1](https://github.com/mr-3mm3/hermes-monitor/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")

Kanban worker health in the Desktop status bar — live activity per running card with stall and loop detection (same tool + same arguments repeated), plus a compact per-provider quota readout (the related ai-usage-tracker plugin covers quota windows as a standalone feature). Zero model tokens. Disclosure — opens HERMES\_HOME/kanban.db and each profile's state.db read-only for worker activity; for quota chips it reads every Hermes profile's credential pool (each profile's auth.json, with that profile's .env as secret scope) into read-only snapshots plus DEEPSEEK\_API\_KEY from the environment or .env files, and calls Hermes' own account-usage fetchers for each configured provider (Anthropic, Codex, OpenRouter, DeepSeek at https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance, and any provider plugin exposing fetch\_account\_usage), sending each entry's own token only to its own provider. The plugin never refreshes or persists a credential; on a Codex HTTP 401, Hermes core may refresh the active profile's matching Codex token via OpenAI's token endpoint and rewrite that profile's auth.json. No other network egress.

### [operations](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/operations)

[★ 1](https://github.com/c-pompa/operations-hermes-desktop-plugin/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")

A Hermes Desktop page for running a fleet - topology, model traffic, handoffs, traces, merge requests and conformance checks in one place. Disclosure — reads hermes-metrics-dash's <hermes root>/metrics/metrics.db, the kanban board, every profile's config.yaml (plugin enable state, rolectl-mcp entries, default model) and plugin-data/gitlab-mr/device-aliases.json, all read-only; calls your GitLab (host and token from the plugin settings or GITLAB\_HOST/GITLAB\_TOKEN), the local model router (MODEL\_ROUTER\_URL, default 127.0.0.1:8867) and LM Studio (LMSTUDIO\_URL, default 127.0.0.1:1234); runs git status/rev-parse/ls-files in the project folders it checks and shows matching lines (including any keys found) on the page. Page buttons create, assign, schedule, unblock and close kanban cards and start their workers at once, write <hermes root>/conformance/conformance.yaml, and "Propose a rule" pushes a branch and opens a merge request on the standard's GitLab project. A hook on every kanban dispatcher tick starts cards scheduled from the page; with alert\_target set it posts new attention items through hermes send; with drift\_action: automatic it files and starts a fix card for drift\_profile for each drifting host with a verified report (at most daily) carrying the standard's remediate commands. With Activity summaries on (off by default), Activity sentences and each "Explain this session" click send log lines and trace details to the model set for the operations\_summary auxiliary task.

### [waypoint](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/waypoint)

[★ 1](https://github.com/mochiNJ/hermes-waypoint/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")

Session status for Hermes Desktop: a thin bar next to every sidebar session with four states — Working (remembers your next step), Waiting on someone (who/what plus a follow-up reminder), Done (outcome plus a fresh-start handoff) and untracked. Suggests 3 next steps per session (instant quick ideas from the chat, opt-in AI ideas from the auxiliary model, priority colours) with one-click Ask, a Power up button that asks a strong model for sharper ideas on demand, and Mark complete to stop suggestions. Adds a Status Board page (columns, follow-ups due, stale sessions, archive all done), triage of untracked sessions, a resume banner above the composer, a status-bar counter, a daily summary, palette commands and English/Arabic (RTL). SDK-only: session-row slots, a route, sidebar nav, status bar, composer banner, palette. Disclosure — no network calls of its own (all model calls go through Hermes llm.oneshot); AI next-step suggestions are OFF by default; when enabled, after new replies (at most every 90 s) the plugin sends the focused session's last ~12 user/assistant messages (≤ ~7,000 chars) plus its title and the user's notes to the auxiliary task title\_generation (Hermes default "auto" = your main model); Power up runs only when pressed — also with AI suggestions off — and sends a longer excerpt (last ~20 messages, ≤ ~12,000 chars) to the plugin's own auxiliary tasks waypoint\_ideas / waypoint\_ideas\_2 (registered by \_\_init\_\_.py; unset they resolve to "auto" = your main model) or, for "My chat model", to the open session's model; an optional automatic big idea (off by default) uses the same choice at most every 10 minutes; Power up call log (2.5.0): the Python half also registers two observe-only hooks (pre\_auxiliary\_call, post\_auxiliary\_call) that ignore every auxiliary task except waypoint\_ideas / waypoint\_ideas\_2 and, for those, write one line per call to the user's own Hermes log (logs/agent.log) and append a record to <HERMES\_HOME>/plugin-data/waypoint/power-calls.jsonl (rolls over at ~1 MB): model, provider, reasoning effort, response time, token counts (logged as 'unknown' with a reason when Hermes reports none), finish reason and status — never prompt, message or reply text, nothing leaves the machine, and the hooks never modify a call; reads session history (session.history) and titles (session.list); statuses, notes and cached suggestion text are kept in desktop plugin storage; archives sessions only when you press Archive (undo offered) or confirm "Archive N done" on the board (no undo; sessions stay under Archived); posts in-app and native OS notifications for due reminders and a once-a-day local summary; writes composer drafts only on Ask / Insert / Start fresh session and never sends them.

### [codex-account-switch](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/codex-account-switch)

[★ 0](https://github.com/SmelterLabs/hermes-account-switcher/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")

Windows desktop plugin that switches which Codex login and which Claude subscription account every local Hermes profile uses, with one idle-only, verified restart of Hermes Desktop and the gateway. Refuses while any profile is busy, restores the previous selection if a step fails, and writes a receipt that says whether the switch took effect. Disclosure — Windows only. A switch rewrites, through Hermes's own commands, the Codex credential order in every profile's auth.json and the CLAUDE\_SUBSCRIPTION\_DIRECTSDK\_CONFIG\_DIR line in every profile's .env, so every profile that has the plugin enabled spends the same selected Codex login and the same Claude login (one Hermes-owned claude-auth folder; no token is copied between profiles). It reads Codex tokens from each profile's auth.json and the Desktop backends' dashboard session token from their process environment, then closes Hermes Desktop and stops and restarts the gateway once both report idle (work started in the seconds after that check is cut off). It sends the target Codex token to OpenAI's usage endpoint and Claude login tokens to Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint (also when the setup screen opens); if the target Claude login has expired it first runs the claude CLI once so the CLI renews its own token, which rotates that login's refresh token. No telemetry and no automatic account rotation.

### [field-academy](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/field-academy)

[★ 0](https://github.com/Dgardenhire/hermes-field-academy/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")

Learn Hermes by doing real work. Four paths (Messenger, Traveler, Crossroads, Boundary Keeper) climb Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced to a capstone on a problem of your own, and a fifth, Guide, covers setting Hermes up for a client: practice labs built from made-up data, a proposal, one real service run by a scheduled job for several days, a recovery drill, and a review signed by a reviewer you choose. Every mission ends with a check on something you made; your own Hermes scores your written answers in a new chat; passed missions come back for short spaced reviews; and at the end of a path you can create a Field Record, your own self-issued learning record. Field Academy is an independent community plugin. It is not made, issued or endorsed by Nous Research. Disclosure — no network calls (a source link opens in your browser only when you click it); no credentials, telemetry, shell commands, background processes or self-updates; registers six tools, two hooks, the /academy command and one skill: pre\_llm\_call may add one sentence offering a practice to the user message, only in interactive desktop, TUI and CLI sessions, and post\_tool\_call records which tool was used; pressing Try it or a scoring button opens a new chat and sends the practice or scoring prompt there (on an older Hermes it goes to the clipboard instead); the Desktop page calls gateway list methods only (session.list, cron.manage list, skills.manage list, tools.list, mcp.catalog, commands.catalog, setup.runtime\_check); stores progress, pasted documents, practice labs, review packets and saved Field Records in $HERMES\_HOME/plugin-data/field-academy/; reads a file you name (UTF-8 text, max 5 MiB) and hashes a recording you name without copying it; Guide labs write and check made-up .env and auth.json files inside its own labs folder (refusing to build in a real Hermes home) and never read Hermes's real ones; on the Guide path reads Hermes's run-history database read-only and immutable, jobs.json and up to 25 log files (2 MiB each), keeping only timestamps for the job you name, and reads install-stamp.json for the Hermes version; no private Hermes imports.

### [hermes-call-ledger](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-call-ledger)

[★ 0](https://github.com/skappafrost/hermes-call-ledger/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")

Per-call cost ledger for Hermes Desktop: every model call Hermes makes is recorded from the observer hooks (provider, model, tokens, duration, outcome) and paired with the charge the billing provider actually took; works with no billing account, priced by Hermes' own estimate where the price book knows the model. English or Vietnamese; dong or dollars. Disclosure — three observer hooks (post\_api\_request, post\_auxiliary\_call, api\_request\_error) record per-call metadata from every profile in the install (session id, platform, task, provider, model, token counts, duration, finish reason, context length; never prompt, response or tool-argument text) into one shared SQLite ledger at <install root>/plugin-data/call-ledger/calls.sqlite, and import this plugin's own older per-profile ledgers into it once. It caches the vilao.ai model list there and the USD-to-VND rate under the active profile's plugin-data/call-ledger. Network is GET-only: vilao.ai (wallet balance, per-request usage, consumer keys) with VILAO\_PAT read through Hermes's secret scope (vilao issues one full-scope token per account, including wallet writes; this plugin only reads), the public vilao.ai model list with no credential, and open.er-api.com for the dollar rate. The first full billing pull pages back through up to ten years of the account's usage. Nothing runs while the Desktop page is closed. Derived from hermes-resetwatch (Adolanium, MIT).

Fleet control for Hermes Desktop: live statusbar chip (N/M IOWAP nodes online), a draggable fleet pane, a full fleet page (status, load, queue depth, capabilities per node, activity) and a tasks page that submits to any task-type capability on the fleet and tracks submitted tasks live (per-stage status dots, result previews, artifacts). Data stays local via the local node-cli against your own IOWAP relay; agent sessions join through an optional iowap-task bridge into a shared track store. Disclosure — the dashboard backend runs the local node-cli (the IOWAP node client from github.com/iowap-org/iowap-node) to read your relay's node list, capabilities and task results, and to submit tasks you start from the Tasks page to nodes on your IOWAP fleet. Relay health also goes through the local node-cli (\`server health\`) — the plugin itself makes no raw HTTP calls to the relay; node identity comes from the node's own ~/.relay state files. Tracked task ids are stored in your Hermes home under plugin-data/iowap/.

[★ 0](https://github.com/freefate258/quote-ask/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")

Codex-style ask-about-selection for Hermes Desktop: select text anywhere in a conversation, and a small pill appears above the selection offering Quote & ask — the selection lands in the message composer as a Markdown quote with the caret on the line below, ready for your question — or Copy, which puts the same Markdown quote on the clipboard. A command-palette entry does the same without the pill. Desktop-only (desktop/plugin.js inside the plugin SDK surface): no agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars, nothing written to disk, nothing persisted. Disclosure — reads window.getSelection() and the selection rectangle; serializes the selection to Markdown (fenced code with its language, nested lists, bold/italic, links), cut at 4000 characters; writes the draft through host.composer (getDraft/setDraft, falling back to insertText, then ctx.os.writeClipboard) and focuses the composer; ignores selections made inside the composer itself and hides on collapse, scroll or Escape. No network calls, no credentials, no telemetry.

Disclosure — stores the value in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600) and adds the name to terminal.env\_passthrough, so $NAME is available to the terminal tool; the model can still read the value with its own tools (cat .env, echo $NAME). Keeps secrets out of chat/prompt context and redacts verbatim output of credential-shaped values; it is not a boundary against a model that deliberately reads it. Adds a static system-prompt section and a /secret command. Imports private core helpers read-only (\_config\_profile\_scope, \_is\_hermes\_provider\_credential, \_CONFIG\_LOCK).

\
[★ 0](https://github.com/strnadchristopher/hermes-wallpaper-theme/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
A Hermes Desktop theme that follows your wallpaper. Reads Pywal's ~/.cache/wal/colors.json by default, or any palette JSON you point it at (settings page or ~/.config/hermes-wallpaper-theme/config.json), derives a palette with checked contrast floors and repaints live when the file changes. Optional glass mode paints a translucent background for native window materials or compositor blur. Disclosure — the desktop half uses only @hermes/plugin-sdk; the palette file is read by the package's own backend route (dashboard/plugin\_api.py, GET /api/plugins/wallpaper-theme/palette, mounted once the plugin is in plugins.enabled), polled every 3 seconds with a change stamp. That route reads only JSON files inside the user's home directory (or XDG\_\*\_HOME) under 256 KiB and returns colour fields only, never raw file text. No network calls, no shell commands, no credentials, no telemetry.\

### [hermes-lcm-x](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-lcm-x)\
\
[★ 60](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/stargazers "60 GitHub stars")\
\
Lossless memory for long sessions: LCM-X keeps every turn in a local store instead of compacting it away, and the agent can search and expand it. The store is local SQLite (lcm.db) with a recoverable DAG of summaries over it and 15 lcm\_\* tools for search, recall and expansion. Select it with context.engine: lcm-x. Upgrading from hermes-lcm (breaking in v0.24.0): stop Hermes, then in plugins.enabled replace hermes-lcm with hermes-lcm-x and run exactly one LCM copy (the install script prints the steps; the old engine name lcm still resolves with a deprecation warning); lcm.db and the lcm: config block are unchanged. Summaries use the model Hermes is configured with. Disclosure — optional semantic recall (embeddings\_enabled, off by default) sends message text to the embedding provider you configure (Voyage via VOYAGE\_API\_KEY, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama), and once enabled new summaries are embedded automatically in the background; in-process FastEmbed keeps it on the machine after a one-time model download. For known cloud providers the provider-bound copy is privacy-transformed by default (LCM\_EMBEDDING\_PRIVACY\_ENABLED=false opts out), while lcm.db keeps the raw text. Every turn (user, assistant and tool output) is stored in plaintext in lcm.db (secret redaction at rest is opt-in), and oversized tool outputs are by default written as plaintext files under HERMES\_HOME/lcm-large-outputs and replaced in the model's context by recoverable references. The engine also reads Hermes' state.db read-only for session lineage, reads private AIAgent attributes via the call stack on Hermes builds without subagent hooks, and runs git on its own install directory for lcm\_status/lcm\_doctor; tiktoken may fetch its BPE file on first use.\
\

### [hyatlas](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hyatlas)\
\
[★ 29](https://github.com/tuancookiez-hub/HyAtlas-Memory/stargazers "29 GitHub stars")\
\
HyAtlas v4 — self-hosted 8-layer memory provider backed by a pure-Go single-binary server you run yourself (chromem-go vectors, in-process BGE-small embeddings, hybrid vector + keyword search, bitemporal knowledge graph with source citations). Embeddings, the vector index and stored memories stay local. Ships agent tools (hyatlas\_status/search/recent/add), a \`hermes hyatlas\` CLI, a Desktop pane with a starmap graph view, and a web dashboard. Disclosure — requires the separate hyatlas-go server, installed by the user. The plugin never downloads or bundles it, and it talks only to the configured server (default 127.0.0.1:19528). Embeddings and stored memories stay local. Extraction is opt-in: the server has no default LLM endpoint and makes no LLM call until HYATLAS\_LLM\_BASE, HYATLAS\_LLM\_MODEL and HYATLAS\_LLM\_KEY are all set. The repo installer pre-fills a free Nous Portal endpoint that Enter accepts, but nothing is sent until you also enter a key. Once configured, each turn's user and assistant text goes to that endpoint (not tool output or context summaries; capped at 12,000 characters). In the default ultra mode the server also sends topic-grouped batches of up to 50 stored facts to it every 6 hours (every 20 minutes while earlier batches are still pending) and supersedes (hides but keeps) the facts the model marks merged or stale, recording a reason for each drop. It also records relations corroborated across turns in the local knowledge graph (HYATLAS\_CONSOLIDATE\_GRAPH=off disables that). In pro and ultra modes it also sends each owner's open intentions and recent summaries to rewrite a short Now page, at most every 15 minutes (HYATLAS\_NOW\_EVERY). An optional HYATLAS\_LLM\_FALLBACK\_MODEL, tried only when a primary call fails, receives the same text; it is sent the primary key only when it uses the same host. HYATLAS\_MODE=lite makes no LLM call. Server endpoints that rewrite stored data are off unless the server runs with HYATLAS\_ADMIN=on. The spawned server gets an allowlisted environment (OS essentials plus HYATLAS\_\*), not the agent's keys. auto\_start is off by default; when on, Hermes starts the server as soon as it loads the plugin, and a server started by auto\_start or \`hermes hyatlas start\` keeps running after Hermes exits until \`hermes hyatlas stop\`. On Windows, if a hyatlas-go.ps1 launcher is configured, \`hermes hyatlas start/stop\` runs it; the repo's sample launcher reads your Nous token from Hermes auth.json and points extraction at the Nous Portal. No telemetry.\
\

\
[★ 28](https://github.com/RohiRIK/OpenLtm/stargazers "28 GitHub stars")\
\
Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional semantic recall via a local llama.cpp embedding server. MIT licensed. Disclosure — local SQLite in HERMES\_HOME; runs git config to read the repo remote; memory text goes to Gemini or OpenAI embeddings, or to the llama.cpp server URL you set (default 127.0.0.1:8080), only if selected in openltm.json (default local Ollama)\

Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto\_nap is enabled. ### [holographic](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/holographic)\
\
[★ 13](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic/stargazers "13 GitHub stars")\
\
Local fact-store memory provider: SQLite with FTS5 keyword search (word forms in English, Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Indonesian, German, Hindi, Arabic, Bengali, Italian, Turkish, Polish and Dutch; Russian and English words of the same root at a lower weight, from bundled DerivBase.Ru (Apache-2.0) and Open English Wordnet (CC BY 4.0) pairs; German compounds and German and Spanish irregular verb forms from bundled Wikidata Lexemes tables (CC0); Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai by character n-grams, Chinese also split into words with jieba's dictionary (MIT), Traditional and Simplified Chinese compared as one through a bundled OpenCC table (Apache-2.0), Japanese spelling variants through SudachiDict's (Apache-2.0); synonyms through keywords the agent gives when it stores a fact), trust scores, entities with aliases and HRR (holographic reduced representation) recall, with no API key, network or model calls unless the optional search by meaning (embeddings: on, off by default) is switched on. The provider that shipped in-tree as plugins/memory/holographic, with the same provider name, config (plugins.hermes-memory-store) and memory\_store.db, so \`hermes update\` moves existing users onto it; the schema change is additive and older versions keep working on the file. Taken over from Nous Research's handoff copy (NousResearch/hermes-plugin-holographic) and maintained by itpartypattaya; since 0.1.1 it fixes probe/reason/related/contradict, non-atomic writes and the never-written retrieval\_count, gates recall by relevance without repeats, flags duplicates and conflicts when a fact is added, and honours the provider contract (read-only subagent contexts, hermes\_home, mirror metadata, backup\_paths); since 0.8.0 it keeps the history of every fact (change / end / correct / revert, search and list as\_of a date) and \`forget\` erases a fact with all its versions from the file; since 0.16.0 a name guessed from a fact's text must be shaped like one and stays provisional until a second fact or a person confirms it, and entities can be renamed or deleted (the facts stay). Disclosure — local only unless the optional search by meaning is switched on: reads and writes one SQLite file per profile ($HERMES\_HOME/memory\_store.db unless db\_path says otherwise), or with scope: user / chat / thread one file per user or chat in holographic-users/ or holographic-chats/ next to it; each fact version records where it was written (platform, chat type, chat and thread id, session id, the turn author's id and display name, and whether the person said it or the agent inferred it; never chat titles), shown in full by list, history and export and not in recall unless recall\_source: short (date, display name, this or another chat); each confirmation of a fact by a person keeps its time, session id and that person's id (no text); forget deletes that and the confirmations with the fact and keeps only an HMAC of the text, keyed by a random key stored in the same file, as a tombstone; delete\_entity removes a name, its aliases and links from the entity index (never a fact) and keeps an HMAC of each name the same way (not of an alias only a fact's text gave, which goes without one), and both rewrite the file so freed pages keep no copy; the first writable open after an upgrade that changes the extraction rules relinks the facts to their entities under the new rules (stores up to 2,000 facts and 500,000 characters; larger ones on fact\_store rebuild\_entities), changing only the names it guessed and their links, never a fact, a declared name or an alias someone gave; subagents never write, but a cron job's explicit fact\_store / fact\_feedback calls do unless cron\_writes: false (on by default); no subprocesses or telemetry, and no network calls or credentials unless embeddings: on (off by default): then the text of facts, and of messages and fact\_store search queries that are not greetings, goes to the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint the user configures, also after cron turns while cron\_writes is on (embedding\_url; https, plain http only to localhost, a private or link-local address, or a local host name such as one without a dot or ending in .local), with the key read from the environment variable the user names (embedding\_key\_env, OPENAI\_API\_KEY unless set, sent as a Bearer token to whatever embedding\_url is configured, never stored in config) and no redirects followed; facts that recall would not inject, and facts and messages that look like they hold a secret (checked by pattern, best effort), are not sent; the vectors are kept in the same file (table fact\_embeddings), deleted with their fact by forget / end / remove and all of them by the next writable session after the option is switched off; the provider keeps what it received under its own terms; the bundled language dictionaries are gzip-compressed plain-text word lists; with auto\_extract on (off by default) user sentences that state a preference or decision are stored.\

### [limbic](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/limbic)\
\
[★ 8](https://github.com/dyiapanis/limbic/stargazers "8 GitHub stars")\
\
Self-organising memory provider (MemoryProvider ABC): local SQLite (WAL) with sqlite-vec KNN + FTS5 hybrid recall, adaptive trust scoring, activation maturation, interference-based forgetting, NLI-based correction detection and synaptic atrophy. No LLM cost — all lifecycle mechanisms are deterministic. The optional inline chat recall indicator is off by default (recall\_indicator in limbic.yaml) and memory injection works identically either way. Recall is confidence-gated: when nothing clears the calibration floor, recall abstains (no\_confident\_match) instead of surfacing near-misses, and the agent answers from what it knows without attributing anything to memory. Tools (remember/recall) and lifecycle hooks dispatch via the MemoryManager from the registered provider — this entry registers a MemoryProvider only, so provides\_tools/provides\_hooks are empty. Disclosure — on first primary session start downloads ~1.0GB of ONNX models (Arctic Embed 2.0 L int8 embedding, ~570MB; MiniLMv2 NLI, ~430MB, on first contradiction check) from huggingface.co at pinned commits with hash checks into ~/.cache/limbic/ (outside HERMES\_HOME); at every model load, every file in those cache folders that is not in the pinned manifest is deleted — including unrelated files if you point embedding/nli cache\_dir at a shared folder — which reclaims stale orphans from prior versions (e.g. an older fp32 cache of ~2.2GB); the memory database is never touched; spaCy NER models are not downloaded and must be installed manually for entity extraction; memory stays local in limbic.db under HERMES\_HOME, and hermes backup adds VACUUM snapshots under HERMES\_HOME/backups; no telemetry. Stores created or reindexed on 0.6.0+ record the embedder that produced their vectors and report stale\_embedder=true after an embedder change until \`hermes limbic reindex\`; stores from 0.5.x keep serving their fp32 vectors unflagged until reindexed. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (commercial use requires a separate license).\
\

### [hermes-dreaming](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-dreaming)\
\
[★ 6](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/stargazers "6 GitHub stars")\
\
Nightly deterministic memory consolidation ("dreaming"): corroborates candidate facts with what humans actually said on distinct days, proposes the few worth keeping with a verbatim edit anchor, asks whether stale memory entries still hold, and wakes the agent only when there is work — including a memory file close to its char limit. Fact sources: the holographic store, a SQLite or JSONL export, or none. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars. Disclosure — scripts make no network or LLM calls and open state.db and every fact store read-only (SQLite mode=ro); they also read Hermes config.yaml's memory/timezone keys and the holographic plugin's db\_path/scope/cron\_writes/min\_trust\_threshold (the floor recall applies, so a rejected fact is only reported when the store still trusts it) and, to say so in install.py --check, embeddings/mirror\_memory\_writes, the pending/memory approval queue, cron/jobs.json (to find their own jobs) and — only when chat\_stores is set, with holographic scope user/chat/thread — the per-chat databases next to the store (counts of every one; facts of the chats listed in promote\_from). The user-run installer copies three gate scripts into $HERMES\_HOME/scripts, seeds $HERMES\_HOME/dreaming.json and, through Hermes' cron Python API, creates (or with --rebind re-points) two agent cron jobs bound to this plugin's own skill with only the memory toolset, plus one no\_agent job (every 15 min, no model) that reads the fact stores to keep a hash index of diary lines and, for facts holographic >= 0.8.0 has forgotten, rewrites the dream's own cache files and diary without them and deletes the output files of the dream's own cron jobs that mention them (by id or verbatim text); with a chat --deliver target the reports are attached as a session you can reply to. The agent runs send recent human messages (up to 200 / 40k chars, each with its chat type and sender id) and fact snippets to your configured model; state goes to $HERMES\_HOME/cache and a diary to $HERMES\_HOME/memories/DREAMS.md (configurable); memory files are changed by the agent only through the regular memory tool, and with the holographic provider it also adds candidate facts via fact\_store (with holographic >= 0.8.0 also change / end / correct / forget, the last three only on a human's own answer; forget is irreversible), lowers trust on human-rejected facts via fact\_feedback, with holographic >= 0.15.0 raises trust (fact\_feedback confirmed, +0.05, at most 10 facts a night) on facts people repeated on two or more different days and, when keywords.enabled is set (off by default), adds search keywords to facts via fact\_store update.\

### [qdrant-memory](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/qdrant-memory)\
\
[★ 6](https://github.com/cnkang/hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory/stargazers "6 GitHub stars")\
\
Durable native memory for Hermes with LLM fact extraction. Conversations are distilled by the Hermes-configured LLM into searchable memories — facts, preferences and decisions with deduplication and importance — instead of storing turns verbatim, and are kept in Qdrant (embedded, self-hosted Server, or Qdrant Cloud) with configurable embeddings (default: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b at 2560 dimensions). The plugin registers a native MemoryProvider plus four scoped tools: qdrant\_memory\_search, qdrant\_memory\_add, qdrant\_memory\_update and qdrant\_memory\_delete. A SQLite WAL admission ledger makes every write idempotent and replayable across restarts with fail-closed recovery; scoped inventory, portable export and scope-aware deletion (list/export/delete-all with explicit single-agent vs all-agents semantics) ship in the same CLI, and \`migrate mem0\` imports existing Mem0 exports with resumable, verifiable runs. Disclosure — memory text is stored in the configured Qdrant store (embedded files under <HERMES\_HOME>/qdrant-memory/qdrant by default, or the Server/Cloud URL you set), and memory text plus each turn's recall query are sent as plain text to the configured embedding endpoint (default local Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434; an OpenAI-compatible remote endpoint can be configured, and keyed endpoints must use HTTPS). Disclosure — after each primary-agent turn, at session end and before context compression, conversation text goes to the LLM configured in Hermes through the Hermes plugin LLM facade (a provider/model override needs the plugin's Hermes trust grant) to extract facts and to compare near-duplicate memories; that LLM may be a remote provider. Disclosure — the provider is selected with memory.provider: qdrant-memory; its settings live in <HERMES\_HOME>/qdrant-memory.json (0600, secrets stripped on save). QDRANT\_URL, QDRANT\_API\_KEY and EMBEDDING\_API\_KEY are read through the Hermes secret scope, but an api\_key written by hand into qdrant-memory.json takes precedence, and \`migrate mem0\` reads the source Qdrant endpoint and any api\_key from <HERMES\_HOME>/mem0.json or --source-config. Disclosure — state lives under <HERMES\_HOME>/qdrant-memory/ (embedded store, SQLite WAL ledger, lock files); the ledger holds raw turn text and pre-compression transcripts until they are processed, and failed items until retried, then scrubs the bodies. Disclosure — single-writer design: a local ownership lock excludes a second writer to the same profile destination, and Server/Cloud deployments expect one active writer per scope. Disclosure — deletion removes records and fences pending operations, but is not a forensic secure erase (SQLite WAL pages and backups may retain content).\
\

Vector embeddings are off by default; only with embeddings\_enabled: true (provider) or ENTROPICMEM\_EMBEDDINGS=1 / query --semantic (CLI) and the optional sentence-transformers extra installed does first use download all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights from huggingface.co; otherwise the provider has no network egress. The CLI ingest command fetches a user-supplied URL; CLI graph export writes to ./export in the cwd by default and its HTML loads D3/marked from d3js.org and cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened; CLI graph serve starts a loopback HTTP server. entropicmem\_patch\_core edits the plugin's own Core-memory markdown (Persona/User\_Profile), not Hermes core, and is off by default.\

### [nexus](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/nexus)\
\
[★ 2](https://github.com/Neboy72/nexus-memory/stargazers "2 GitHub stars")\
\
Self-hosted long-term memory on Qdrant: automatic per-turn prefetch and write-back, plus recall/remember/forget, guardrail rules and a knowledge graph; Hermes and any MCP-connected agent share one collection. Embeddings run fully local by default (sentence-transformers with Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 1024d, about 1.2 GB from Hugging Face on first use; on Apple Silicon the model is pinned to the CPU, because PyTorch's MPS backend aborts the whole process under two overlapping encodes). A cloud embedder runs only when NEXUS\_EMBEDDING\_PROVIDER names it and its key is present, and a key that merely sits in the environment never selects one. Access levels fail closed: a memory, a protection rule or a graph label without a known level counts as the most restrictive. A local service on 127.0.0.1:9122 serves embeddings and the full MCP toolset; its /embed and /mcp routes demand a per-installation key (service\_auth.key, mode 0600) and reject non-loopback Host/Origin, while the open /healthz answers liveness only. The plugin starts that service when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack, and it keeps running afterwards. Session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint from Hermes config.yaml, and the consolidation daemon to its configured model, which defaults to a cloud model; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; NEXUS\_UPDATE\_CHECK=1 opts into a GitHub release check. Disclosure — when Hermes cannot load the embedding stack (and always on Apple Silicon unless NEXUS\_EMBED\_IN\_HOST=1), the plugin starts \`nexus-memory serve\` on 127.0.0.1:9122 (embeddings, the full Nexus MCP toolset and a consolidation daemon whose default model is a cloud model that receives memory text), and the service keeps running after Hermes exits; its /embed and MCP routes require a per-install key in ~/.nexus-memory/service\_auth.key (0600) and a loopback Host/Origin; session-end fact extraction sends conversation text to the model endpoint in Hermes config.yaml; reads ~/.hermes/.env and config.yaml; state and daily backups under ~/.nexus-memory; opt-in NEXUS\_UPDATE\_CHECK=1 adds a GitHub release check and an upgrade nudge to the system prompt.\

### [hicortex](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hicortex)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/gamaze-labs/hicortex-hermes-plugin/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Shared fleet memory for Hermes agents: every connected agent learns from all other agents connected to the memory, wherever they run. Sessions across machines and harnesses are distilled into one common brain overnight — what one learns, the whole fleet recalls. Pushes a compact per-turn recall index (entries lazy-load via hicortex\_get), injects fresh lessons plus a per-agent standing context block at session start — lesson blocks are delimited and carry an explicit reference-data framing line and provenance header — and exposes the full 9-tool memory surface (search, get, recent, ingest, lessons, index, graph, update, delete) through the shared server. The same server also serves Claude Code, OpenClaw, Pi and opencode agents, so mixed-harness fleets share one brain. Stdlib-only, no pip dependencies. Requires a running Hicortex server (npx @gamaze/hicortex init on any machine); data flow: each user message is sent to your configured Hicortex server for recall (default http://localhost:8787); session distillation runs on the server. Disclosure — sends every user message (and profile name) to your configured Hicortex server each turn for recall, default http://localhost:8787, plain http with a bearer token is accepted for remote servers with a one-time log warning; the server's standing Identity text and lessons are injected into the system prompt; the model can permanently update or delete shared fleet memories via hicortex\_update / hicortex\_delete without confirmation.\

### [qdrant](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/qdrant)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/kuehnberger/hermes-qdrant-memory/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Dense semantic memory for Hermes, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session\_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant\_search, qdrant\_upsert, qdrant\_recall, qdrant\_collect, qdrant\_prepare, qdrant\_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md\_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional recall-indicator display, display.level (off \| summary \| verbose, default off), adds latency and collection to the chat indicator at summary and one numeric line per operation to the log at verbose — numbers and identifiers only, never recalled message text or search-result snippets (the md\_search line also echoes the query you searched — your own input, not recalled content); it is separate from the older top-level progress knob (off \| minimal \| verbose), which gates status events. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is\_available()/check\_backend()/unavailable\_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Optional hybrid dense+sparse RRF search (default off): one config key enables dense+BM25 RRF fusion. A fresh collection declares the sparse vector at creation and an existing dense-only store gets it added in place (Qdrant >= 1.18) with one bundled backfill command; measured +0.024 recall@10 on the LongMemEval 1,000-example benchmark. INT8 quantization is not implemented. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT\_API\_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Hermes secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights (plus the 10 MB Qdrant/bm25 sparse model when hybrid is on) from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding runs on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <HERMES\_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials) and last-operation status in <HERMES\_HOME>/qdrant-status.json. Disclosure — md\_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.hermes/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/hermes\_default, ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/website and any path in the md\_docs\_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md\_ingest.py and lives in <base Hermes home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md\_ingest.py --semantic, and md\_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate hermes\_md\_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT\_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Hermes process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process). Disclosure — the bundled scripts/backfill\_memory.py (run by hand; a dry run unless --yes) reads a profile's Hermes session database (<profile>/state.db, read-only) and copies every stored user, assistant and tool message from every session source (cli, cron, subagent, gateway), in 2,000-character chunks, into the collection at the url in qdrant.json (default http://localhost:6333); nothing reads state.db unless you run it.\
\

[★ 0](https://github.com/dexio-wiki/hermes-plugin/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Dexio shared-wiki memory. Before each turn, the pages of your Dexio wiki that match the user's message; tools to search, read and write the pages your other agents and team also use. Nothing is captured automatically: no transcripts or turn logs. Standard library only; no background threads or local services. Disclosure — with DEXIO\_API\_KEY set, the first 300 characters of each user message go to the Dexio server (default app.dexio.wiki, or DEXIO\_URL) as a search query, tool arguments and the agent's profile name go there on tool calls, and the model is prompted to write, overwrite and edit pages in a wiki shared with the user's team and other agents, without a confirmation step.\

### [gbrain-pointer](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/gbrain-pointer)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/praggybuilds/hermes-gbrain-pointer/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Read-only memory.provider for GBrain (garrytan/gbrain, MIT; not affiliated). After each non-trivial turn it searches a GBrain MCP server (\`gbrain serve --http\`) in the background and injects up to the configured limit (3 by default, capped at 10) of \`\[source:slug\] title\` pointers into the next turn as fallible background context. It never writes to GBrain and adds no tools or hooks. Disclosure — after each non-trivial turn, the first 500 characters of your message are sent to GBRAIN\_MCP\_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:3131/mcp; plain http to a non-loopback host is refused unless GBRAIN\_POINTER\_ALLOW\_HTTP=1), and the profile's GBrain OAuth client id and secret go to that server's /token endpoint. Redirects and proxy settings are ignored. Only the slug, title and source id of up to 10 results are kept and injected into the next turn as background context; rows GBrain flags as suspected injection are skipped. Tokens and pointers stay in memory only. It never writes to GBrain; no other network calls, no telemetry.\
\

[★ 0](https://github.com/lumberroom/lumberroom-hermes/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
lumberroom memory provider. One durable store shared with every agent you use, recalled on every turn and written through the engine's own memory\_write. Self-hosted open-source engine or lumberroom.cloud; OAuth or a static token. Maintained by the lumberroom team. Disclosure — when active, every non-trivial user message (first 1,000 characters) and the absolute git-root path of the working directory are sent on each turn to the configured lumberroom engine, which defaults to https://mcp.lumberroom.cloud (operated by Cybersapien Technologies, India) unless base\_url names a self-hosted engine; the model is instructed to store decisions, preferences and facts there through memory\_write, the engine's live tool descriptions and server instructions are injected into the system prompt each session, and setup switches off Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md store.\

### [whatsapp-agent-platform](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/whatsapp-agent-platform)\
\
[★ 11](https://github.com/ahtishamdilawar/hermes-whatsapp-agent-platform/stargazers "11 GitHub stars")\
\
Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Nous Research) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Hermes through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under HERMES\_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: Hermes fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under HERMES\_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP\_AGENT\_PLATFORM\_MEDIA\_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message Hermes; WHATSAPP\_AGENT\_PLATFORM\_ALLOWED\_USERS or WHATSAPP\_AGENT\_PLATFORM\_ALLOW\_ALL\_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the Hermes .env; the state file under HERMES\_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.\
\

\
[★ 9](https://github.com/Realmagnum/hermes-max-integration/stargazers "9 GitHub stars")\
\
MAX messenger gateway with polling/webhook, streaming, interactive questions, native attachments, Core voice transcription, optional PNG tables and a Desktop sessions sidebar. Disclosure — sends the bot token and message/file content to the MAX Bot API (platform-api2.max.ru) and MAX upload hosts (\*.max.ru, \*.oneme.ru, \*.okcdn.ru). Inbound attachments are downloaded only for allowlisted senders, with SSRF protection, and cached under HERMES\_HOME. The bundled Russian Trusted Root CA is trusted only by the MAX API/upload clients, not attachment downloads. Its platform hint lets the agent attach local host files to MAX replies via MEDIA paths, and a public output hook adds a filename caption to file-only MAX replies. Webhook mode opens a listener (default 0.0.0.0:8646) that requires a secret and public HTTPS. Polling startup deletes all of the bot's webhook subscriptions. Optional table rendering launches Playwright/Chromium; with MAX\_AUTO\_INSTALL\_PLAYWRIGHT=true it pip-installs playwright==1.62.0 and downloads Chromium (~115 MB). The MAX allowlist does not honour Hermes pairing approvals. No telemetry or self-update.\

### [hermes-mobile](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-mobile)\
\
[★ 4](https://github.com/geniok1980/hermes-mobile-adapter/stargazers "4 GitHub stars")\
\
WebSocket platform for your own mobile, desktop or web app: it talks to the agent directly — text, voice, images, video and documents in both directions, approval/clarify/slash cards answered from the app, streaming edits, typing and avatar state events, cron delivery to a chosen device. On request it also answers command-catalog and model-list frames (commands from the agent's own registry, models from its model inventory) so a client renders command and model pickers from the agent's data instead of bundling a snapshot; auto-push after ready is off by default (MOBILE\_CATALOG\_AFTER\_READY=1). Ships TypeScript and Python SDKs, platform guides and an acceptance checklist. Disclosure — opens a listening WebSocket server (plain ws://, no built-in TLS; 127.0.0.1:8787 by default, the wildcard address only when set, behind a wss proxy) guarded by MOBILE\_TOKEN plus optional per-device tokens; anyone holding an unbound token can chat with the agent, run slash commands and answer the approval and clarify cards of the device id they connect as; device\_id=token entries bind a token to one device. deliver frames are accepted only from loopback peers or MOBILE\_DELIVER\_TOKENS. Inbound media is written under $HERMES\_HOME/mobile-media; secrets are read through Hermes's profile-scoped route; approvals resolve through Hermes's own resolvers; no telemetry, no third-party network calls, no self-update.\

### [radio-dm-gateway](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/radio-dm-gateway)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-radio-dm-gateway/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Answers an allowlisted direct message on your Meshtastic® radio. Disclosure — talks only to the MESHTASTIC\_URL you set, over plain tcp, so channel keys and text travel unencrypted. An empty MESHTASTIC\_ALLOWED\_NODES answers nobody. A channel packet or a direct message without pkiEncrypted is never answered, because a channel key can forge a sender. Allowlisted nodes can prompt the agent, use tools until hermes tools turns them off, and approve one command at a time. An approval question is sent only when its line shows exactly the command /approve will run. A line that still goes out after that send was declined does not let /approve run it, and the next approval is declined once. Each direct message runs an agent turn on your model, and the agent cannot send on its own. No cron job comes with it; one the agent makes stays until hermes cron remove. Hermes main does not load this platform when plugins run in their own process. Node ids, sizes and times go to nodes.json in this profile's plugin-data and stay after uninstall. The message text is not stored. Not tried on a physical radio. Meshtastic® is a registered trademark of Meshtastic LLC. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Meshtastic project.\

[★ 0](https://github.com/rrrrnmtsu/hermes-session-mirror/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Mirrors Hermes Desktop, CLI, TUI and ACP conversations into Discord: one public thread per session in a channel you choose, one post per turn (your message and the reply), so work started on a desktop can be followed from the phone. Posting runs on a background thread and never delays or breaks a turn. Disclosure — register() adds one post\_llm\_call hook; every turn's text (your message and the final reply, not tool calls or outputs) is sent to the Discord REST API (discord.com) using the bot token you configure, after Hermes's redact\_for\_egress plus a local token-pattern filter (fail-closed: nothing is sent if the redactor is unavailable); mentions are disabled. The bot token is read only via agent.secret\_scope.get\_secret (an UnscopedSecretError under multiplexing skips the turn); no external command is ever run. Each turn reads the session's title and source from $HERMES\_HOME/state.db read-only; session-to-thread ids are stored (mode 0600) in $HERMES\_HOME/state/session-mirror.json. The optional \`hermes session-mirror backfill\` CLI command reads $HERMES\_HOME/state.db read-only and replays past sessions through the same redaction. No other files, telemetry or long-running processes beyond one daemon sender thread.\

### [hermes-federated-search](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-federated-search)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/kumaxs/hermes-federated-search/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Federated web search backend (provider name \`federated\`): fans one query out to multiple configured search backends in parallel and returns merged, deduplicated, relevance-ranked results (keyword scoring; optional LLM re-rank with automatic fallback). Phase 2 — official settings-page exposure (config\_schema, six keys) merged with the legacy web.federated block, and per-line multi-card credential pools (environment-variable names only) with automatic failover and host-aligned cooldowns. Phase 3 — a desktop card config page (Settings → Plugins; opt-in via Settings → Skills & Tools → Plugins): one card per line, two-level membership checkboxes (backends / credentials), add/remove lines and keys, a per-line Key rotation strategy (pool\_strategy), an LLM ranker model picker (seventh schema key \`ranker\`), and a current-settings string with paste import; no type picker/badges (\`type\` round-trips verbatim); every edit serializes back to the settings tree (string ↔ UI parity). The LLM re-rank request pins thinking off (\`reasoning\_effort=off\`) and the card page states it. Disclosure — reads the operator's config.yaml (read-only) for its own settings (web.federated and plugins.entries.hermes-federated-search.settings); sends the query to the operator-configured sub-backends (registered providers or custom HTTP endpoints); no telemetry, no subprocesses, no credential storage (key values stay in the runtime environment).\
\

### [skill-retrieval](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/skill-retrieval)\
\
[★ 102](https://github.com/moonlight-lupin/agent-skills/stargazers "102 GitHub stars")\
\
BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm\_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available\_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre\_llm\_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register\_middleware, register\_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt\_builder / agent.skill\_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL\_RETRIEVAL\_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $HERMES\_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.\
\

### [plan-mode](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/plan-mode)\
\
[★ 98](https://github.com/100yenadmin/hermes-plan-mode/stargazers "98 GitHub stars")\
\
Claude Code-style plan mode for Hermes: the agent explores and writes a plan, and edits nothing else until you approve it. It works on every interactive Hermes surface: /plan or /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre\_tool\_call (writes outside .hermes/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) while the agent explores, asks clarifying questions and writes a plan. The agent shows the complete plan, submits it with plan\_mode(submit) and one approval card asks: approve and auto-accept edits, approve and review each file edit (when Hermes approvals are on, every write\_file and patch then gets Hermes' approval prompt with its path and a preview), or keep planning; Other sends feedback, and the revised plan says what changed since the last revision. Once approved, it implements in the same turn and tracks todo\_list progress. To change the plan yourself, keep planning, run /planmode edit, save, then /planmode show and /planmode approve; the text you were shown is saved as an approved snapshot, so later edits to the file do not change the approval. The classic profile (plan\_profile: classic), approval\_card: false and surfaces without a card use Hermes' own approval prompt (gateway buttons, the TUI/Desktop card, the CLI panel or /approve). When yolo or approvals.mode: off would auto-approve, it asks through clarify instead, so a person still decides. By default plans are compact and decision-complete, the lean profile asks at most three targeted questions, and the agent does not commit unless asked (plan\_style, plan\_profile, allow\_commits and plan\_skill settings). Classic CLI enforced on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5), and refused on older builds; 0.21.6 recommended. On the interactive classic CLI, Hermes' inline diff shows a new plan file in full, so the agent does not retype it (write\_once). A report-a-problem skill drafts a bug report and files it with gh only after you approve the draft. Disclosure — plan-mode does not enforce Codex app-server exec/applyPatch or TUI /background and btw side agents. A plan is approved only on its approval card (a clarify question only the plugin issues and checks), through Hermes' own approval prompt, or with /planmode approve. It reads nine groups of internal Hermes seams for session identity, workspace, profile, skills.inline\_shell and the classic CLI's inline diff, each guarded with a documented fallback. It creates .hermes/plans under the session working directory, reads plan files there, saves the approved text of an edited plan as a new file under .hermes/plans/approved, and keeps per-session state in plugin state. It adds a turn note while planning or executing, a ≤200-char system-prompt hint, and a one-line footer to short replies on chat platforms. When a turn ends while a submitted plan still awaits approval and no approval card was answered, it adds one line to that reply on any surface, whatever its length, saying how to approve (unless footer is off). When you pick "Always" on a plan approval or a per-edit review, Hermes core writes a plugin\_rule:plan-mode entry to command\_allowlist in config.yaml; each entry is keyed to one plan revision, so it cannot approve another plan. With allow\_gateway\_injection: true it queues one message to start work after a typed /planmode approve. On TUI, Desktop and hermes serve sessions (lean profile, plan\_once) it reads the visible reply text from post\_api\_request while planning and saves its <proposed\_plan> block as the plan file. On the interactive classic CLI (lean, write\_once) it checks that Hermes printed a newly written plan file in full, then tells the agent not to retype it. Its report-a-problem skill has the agent file to the plugin repository with gh only after the user approves the exact saved draft. The plugin itself makes no network calls, launches no subprocesses and has no self-updater.\
\

### [blackbox](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/blackbox)\
\
[★ 63](https://github.com/umanitek/agent-blackbox/stargazers "63 GitHub stars")\
\
Security for agents: checks every tool call and model request before it runs against a curated, verifiable threat graph (prompt injection, dangerous commands, malicious packages, unsafe skills, phishing and drainer indicators) and local rules that keep an agent away from wallet stores, seed phrases, private keys and exchange API keys. Audit mode records; block mode refuses. Can share privacy-safe threat reports with an open community graph once the user turns sharing on (off by default); community findings only ever flag. Hooks only: no tools, no middleware. Disclosure — hooks see every tool call and model request; \`hermes blackbox setup\` installs Node (via a checksum-pinned nvm installer) if missing, the OriginTrail DKG node from npm (checksum-pinned) and Blazegraph in Docker or Oxigraph, registers the DKG node and the dashboard as login services (systemd/LaunchAgent), and joins the DKG peer-to-peer network; package installs are looked up on api.osv.dev (name and version); community threat reports signed by a local reporter key (threat identifiers, including domains of fetched pages that served a verified injection) are shared to the community graph only after you turn sharing on (off by default); the optional LLM reviewer sends the current turn's user and tool text to OpenAI or Anthropic; \`blackbox attach\` copies the plugin into the Hermes homes/profiles and OpenClaw workspaces you name and enables it in their config (automatic attaching is off unless you set \`auto\_attach: true\`); \`hermes blackbox chat\` creates an \`agent-blackbox\` profile cloned from the current one (config.yaml and .env); the dashboard runs on 127.0.0.1:9700.\

Nothing is downloaded and no npm install runs at any point; node (^20.19 or >=22.12) must already be installed and is launched only by the explicit hermes town start command, bound to 127.0.0.1 only. Runtime state, a 0600 bridge token, a bounded event journal and rotated server logs are written under HERMES\_HOME/hermes-town/runtime/. On start the server also reads HERMES\_HOME/cron/jobs.json (job id and enabled flag only) to place one resident per enabled scheduled job.\
\

### [alans-way-computer](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/alans-way-computer)\
\
[★ 7](https://github.com/capthvnsen/alans-way-agents/stargazers "7 GitHub stars")\
\
Computer-use provider for Hermes: the stock computer\_use tool drives desktop apps on the user's computer through the Alan's Workspace app, and on the VM's own desktop when the computer is offline. Needs the Alan's Way Plugin's workspace setup. Select it with computer\_use.backend: alans-way-computer (the Alan's Way Plugin's setup.sh sets this when it installs the provider; in the catalog flow it prints the command). Disclosure — starts the workspace router from the profile's mcp\_servers.workspace\_browser block (command and args from config.yaml, with a filtered environment plus HERMES\_WORKSPACE\_ALLOW\_DESKTOP\_ACTIONS=1, which lets this private router child serve desktop input) as a long-running node child per session. The filtered environment passes PATH, HOME, locale and OS basics, plus DISPLAY, XAUTHORITY and DBUS\_SESSION\_BUS\_ADDRESS so the router's VM-desktop fallback finds the X display and session bus; no keys or tokens. It talks to the router over stdio (app lists, element trees, screenshots and input actions). The router reaches the user's computer over SSH on the user's tailnet and falls back to the VM's desktop, where it uses xdotool, a screenshot tool and the AT-SPI accessibility bus if they are installed (the provider installs none of them). The provider never takes the focused window on the user's computer, and every input action still goes through Hermes's computer\_use approval gate (cua:\*:background entries in command\_allowlist, which the Alan's Way Plugin's --allow-desktop-actions adds, skip the prompt). The provider itself makes no network calls. On Hermes 0.21.5, which has no provider API, it installs and does nothing. Since 0.21.0, captures keep element numbers stable across action replies on Mac and Windows, fold in changed controls and report removed numbers; a truncated list never treats unseen controls as removed. Linux keeps the whole-tree generation guard, so capture again before acting by number after a change. Action replies describe nearby changes and can mark the effect confirmed. Default som captures still fetch a screenshot to measure the window, but omit it from the model when named controls cover at least 35%; mode vision explicitly includes it and mode ax requests no screenshot. Replies identify the coordinate space and explain locked screens, missing permissions, unreadable or cut trees, hung apps and uncertain outcomes before a retry. Element trees, generation, screenshots' geometry and host OS are session memory, with no new persistent provider state, tools, hooks, middleware, required environment variables or direct network destinations. Browser commit approvals are separate from this provider's unchanged computer\_use approval gate.\
\
