### [hermes-switchyard](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-switchyard)\
\
[★ 7](https://github.com/bgrablin/hermes-switchyard/stargazers "7 GitHub stars")\
\
Jev-powered Hermes plugin for skill/model routing, typed assess, DOM/Cua computer use, adaptive reasoning effort with a per-turn receipt line, and FTS rerank. Disclosure: the default-on adaptive llm\_request sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message to TypeSafe/OpenRouter after Hermes redact\_for\_egress (no history or tool output); greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call; without the Hermes redactor it sends metadata only (disable via adaptive\_reasoning\_effort false). Separate default-on hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters of the current user turn after Hermes redact\_for\_egress, plus skill names, to the same provider; without the redactor it stays local (opt down to local\_only); light turns (greetings, closed acknowledgements, and read-only listings) skip that hosted call by default. Model routing remains advisory. Disclosure — By default, adaptive effort sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message, and hosted skill routing sends up to 4,000 characters plus skill names, to TypeSafe/OpenRouter Jev after Hermes redact\_for\_egress (greetings and light turns stay local). The jev\_session\_search\_rerank and jev\_computer\_use DOM tools send query/card and public-page text using the plugin's own masking. Off unless enabled: evidence prefetch sends source files the user names under evidence\_finder\_root (up to 80 KB), cross-tool stuck advice sends redacted error excerpts, and the switchyard-approvals provider, once selected for auxiliary.approval, sends flagged shell commands and your approval policy to OpenRouter Jev, whose confident verdict can auto-approve them (any failure falls back to a human prompt). /switchyard effort receipt saves the plugin's own setting to config.yaml.\

### [index-network](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/index-network)\
\
[★ 6](https://github.com/indexnetwork/hermes-plugin/stargazers "6 GitHub stars")\
\
Give your agent someone to talk to. Index is the social layer between personal agents. It makes it possible to find the others who share your flavor of weird, no searching or posting needed.\
You're already telling your agent what you're interested in, and what you're secretly tinkering on. We give personal agents the coordination protocol to socialize their humans' intents. They structure mutual intents into opportunities, negotiate on fit, learn from each turn, and surface connections between people who otherwise might've just missed each other. Disclosure — login (browser or \`hermes index login\`) writes INDEX\_SESSION\_TOKEN and INDEX\_API\_URL to the Hermes env. When this install is the selected negotiator (under the gateway, Desktop's backend or the dashboard), a Bun child (INDEX\_BUN, else PATH) runs the pinned bundle with an allowlisted environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, LC\_ALL, TZ plus names in INDEX\_NEGOTIATOR\_ENV\_PASSTHROUGH; never the session token, no .env files) and drives your Hermes model over a loopback bridge; only with plugins.entries.index-network.settings.custom\_negotiator set to true (default off) does the bundle import $HERMES\_HOME/index/negotiator.ts, when it exists, and run it on each turn before the built-in negotiator (code in that file runs with the negotiator's Index API key and model bridge); the plugin mints INDEX\_API\_KEY from the session if it is missing, saves it to the Hermes env and registers the Index MCP server in config.yaml. API traffic goes to protocol.index.network. If INDEX\_EARLY\_NETWORK\_ID is set, confirming onboarding joins that Index network. Negotiation turns are saved as Hermes sessions in a Negotiations project. The 08:00 "Index morning" cron job is off until turned on; when on it wakes the negotiator once per active networked signal, spending model calls and possibly sending outreach. The desktop half ships as desktop/plugin.js and stays off until enabled.\
\

### [telegram-stickers](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/telegram-stickers)\
\
[★ 5](https://github.com/churnast/hermes-telegram-stickers/stargazers "5 GitHub stars")\
\
Lets your agent answer in Telegram with a sticker, the way a person reacts to a joke or good news: four default packs made by Telegram out of the box, then packs you list or send the bot in a direct chat; picked by emoji or by meaning, sent as a reply in the current chat and forum topic, paced per chat, with a per-chat off switch the agent cannot undo. Pace and packs can be set in words in your direct chat. Disclosure: calls only the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org or the configured api\_base) with the gateway's TELEGRAM\_BOT\_TOKEN, read through Hermes' secret scope: getStickerSet for the packs in use (during the first-run setup also from a short background thread, only for a sender Hermes answers, at most 32 at once), sendSticker, and getFile plus one download per sticker for /stickers describe, which the owner starts and which sends each sticker image to the vision model configured in Hermes. A native Telegram handler sees stickers sent to the bot in direct chats (not in groups), skips forwarded ones and keeps pack name, sticker kind and sender id in memory for up to an hour; everyone the bot answers in a direct chat can add packs, up to max\_learned\_packs in all (default 100, 0 for no limit; learn\_packs: false turns learning off). A pre\_llm\_call hook appends fixed text to the user message of Telegram turns: a sticker hint of about 540 characters, a settings note of about 310 characters when the message mentions stickers, or a setup paragraph during the first-run setup. Writes catalog.json, descriptions.json and state.json under plugin-data/telegram-stickers/ and reads Hermes' sticker\_cache.json. No middleware: the sticker tools run through Hermes like any tool. Uses Hermes functions outside the plugin API (tools.vision\_tools.vision\_analyze\_tool, gateway.session\_context.get\_session\_env) and reads the call stack to tell the local CLI or TUI from other callers of /stickers. No shell commands, telemetry or self-update. Anyone the bot answers in a direct chat counts as the owner: they can change pacing, packs, banned stickers and per-chat on/off; the off switch the agent cannot undo holds in groups only.\
\

The 21 troubleshooting skills are not loaded by the plugin: they install separately from the repo as a skills tap, which this entry's pin does not cover.\

### [account-pool](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/account-pool)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/roqianjas/hermes-account-pool/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Run several accounts of one provider in Hermes' credential pool: \`hermes account <provider> <action>\` adds accounts with email verification, shows live usage per account, keeps the least-used account first (fill\_first + a 5-minute balance timer over every provider with accounts), parks accounts for hours or on a weekly schedule, shows which bot is on which account and its tokens at API prices, alerts on dead logins, a full pool or a runaway bot, and can start an idle account's 5-hour window with one tiny request (wake). Adapters for anthropic and openai-codex; generic commands for any pool provider. Optional Accounts page in Hermes Desktop. Linux and Windows. Disclosure — logins stay in Hermes: park holds an entry out of rotation in Hermes' pool (mark\_exhausted\_and\_rotate, reason "parked") and unpark is reset\_status; the plugin's park list holds labels, ids and times only; expired tokens are refreshed by Hermes (try\_refresh\_matching); sign-in, in the terminal and on the Desktop page, runs \`hermes auth add\`; other profiles' accounts are read with read\_credential\_pool. It uses each account's access token as Hermes stores it for live usage and the email check (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and /profile, chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, with the client headers of Hermes' usage fetcher) and for wake (a command, a page button, or the timer after the opt-in \`wake auto-on\`): one one-word request per account through Hermes' Anthropic client or the Codex Responses endpoint, and the account's model list. Telegram alerts through \`hermes send -t telegram\` to the bot's home channel or a chat id kept in account-pool.json; no telemetry. Its session tracker, a post\_api\_request hook, runs in every profile and writes labels, ids and token counts only. \`setup\` writes plugins.enabled of every profile, links the plugin into every profile, removes the retired account-pool-tracker (\`hermes plugins remove\`) and, with --timer, adds a systemd user timer (Linux) or a Task Scheduler task for the user (Windows, no admin rights). Runs systemctl --user and notify-send (Linux), schtasks, powershell.exe and taskkill (Windows), hermes config set, hermes auth add/remove, hermes send, hermes plugins remove; reads every profile's config.yaml and state.db (read-only), the gateway config (whether the Telegram bot has a home channel) and /proc on Linux. The command registers in the default profile only and provides no tools. Live usage, the email check and wake send each account's own access token from Hermes' pool straight to its vendor with Claude Code (anthropic) and Codex CLI (openai-codex) client headers. The session tracker reads the running agent's current pool account (label and id only) by scanning Python thread frames for Hermes' private \_credential\_pool. On the first run after 3.x it moves parked logins from account-pool-parked.json back into Hermes' pool and deletes that file.\
\

### [agent-janitor](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/agent-janitor)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/ZidoCode/agent-janitor/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Process hygiene for agent machines — finds the background processes your agent left behind (dev servers, tunnels, watchers, nohup jobs) using evidence signals (ppid=1 reparent, port listener via /proc/net/tcp{,6}, dev-server traits, TTL exceeded) and attributes them to the originating tool call via agent-ledger's ledger when present. Dry-run by default: nothing is killed until you write policy\_mode=enforce; system daemons and host/VM management agents are exempt by name, a user-editable whitelist covers your real infrastructure, and each kill re-reads the cmdline first (SIGTERM, 2s, SIGKILL with PID-reuse check). stdlib-only, fails open. Disclosure — inside Hermes it only appends terminal commands that look like they start background work (first 300 characters, which can include inline secrets) to plugin-data/agent-janitor/spawns.jsonl, and reads agent-ledger's ledger.db read-only when present. Killing is a separate CLI you run yourself (janitor\_cli.py sweep): after you write "enforce" to plugin-data/agent-janitor/policy\_mode it sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to every process re-parented to PID 1 for over a minute that is not on its built-in exempt list or your whitelist, whoever started it (for example a tmux server or a nohup'd hermes gateway), including other users' processes when run as root. Dry-run first; the dry-run list is the kill list.\
\

Disclosure — spawns the vendor devin CLI from PATH or cli\_path (devin acp, devin acp --cloud, devin --print, devin auth status, devin models list); the CLI edits files and runs shell commands in a folder the model picks (any folder unless allowed\_roots is set) under the configured permission mode (accept-edits/smart auto-allow edits, dangerous auto-allows everything and needs allow\_dangerous: true), and talks to Cognition's servers; Devin Cloud runs use Cognition-managed permissions that Hermes does not gate. Every model-initiated launch goes through Hermes approval; follow-ups typed on a Desktop run card and answers to Devin's prompts on the card start or allow actions on that click without a Hermes prompt (unanswered card prompts are denied after 300 s by default). Uses the existing Devin CLI login and stores no credentials; Hermes provider, bot and tool secrets are stripped from the child environment (extra\_env is passed as set). Background runs continue after the turn up to their timeout and post Devin's output back into the conversation as a message when they finish. Run history (prompts, diffs, command output) and model preferences are saved under plugin-data/devin unless persist\_runs is off. Independent community add-on, not affiliated with Cognition.\

### [evalroute](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/evalroute)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/keppy/hermes-plugin-evalroute/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Route a task to the right (model, reasoning effort) arm before you start. Classifies the task into a lane, prints a provenance-carrying route card, and installs per-model reasoning-effort defaults. Strong rules run locally; weak-signal classification calls the host LLM and consumes tokens. The separate harness and shim can make paid provider calls when explicitly run; no plugin-owned credentials. Disclosure — weak-signal task classification sends the task text to your active Hermes model via the host LLM facade (token cost). The model-callable tool, /route, /rate and observed /model and /reasoning commands append task text and command args to a local ledger at <HERMES\_HOME>/evalroute/labels.jsonl. "hermes evalroute install-routes" rewrites agent.reasoning\_overrides in config.yaml when you run it. The bundled harness and Hermes shim are never run by the plugin. When run by hand they make paid provider calls, execute model-generated code on the host via shell checkers, and run hermes -z with approvals bypassed. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute sync" (run by hand) downloads the route table from the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel into HERMES\_HOME and route cards then show that dataset's text; "hermes evalroute dispatch" (run by hand) spawns a single-query hermes chat on the routed model (Nous provider by default) — or, with --runner claude-code, a \`claude -p\` (Claude Code) process under the user's own Claude account, whose per-run cost is recorded in the local sidecar — with the brief as its query, inheriting the current environment except HERMES\_YOLO\_MODE (the worker never inherits --yolo; its approvals follow approvals.single\_query\_mode, default deny), and writes its report and a .dispatch.json sidecar beside the brief. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute contribute" (run by hand only) refuses to run unless evalroute.contribute: true is set in config.yaml, and then uploads redacted outcome rows only — lane, routed arm, confirmed arm, verdict, method, facet counts, ISO week and an HMAC-SHA256 task hash; never task text, notes, paths or the salt — to the user's own path (contributed/<hf-username>/) in the Hugging Face dataset keppy/evalroute-flywheel using the user's existing huggingface\_hub login; "--dry-run" prints the exact rows and sends nothing; the per-install salt stays local in <HERMES\_HOME>/evalroute/contribute.salt. Since evalroute 0.9.1 (schema 2) the same upload also carries lane-correction rows as lane pairs (from\_lane, to\_lane, method, week) with no task text, plus the max\_turns value and harness name the arm ran under. Disclosure — "hermes evalroute install-encoder <dir\|owner/name>" (run by hand only) downloads a small text-classification model (the default id keppy/evalroute-lane-encoder is a 146 MB ModernBERT fine-tune on the Hugging Face Hub) into <HERMES\_HOME>/evalroute/encoder/ and from then on "hermes evalroute route" runs it locally, offline, to classify the task when the keyword rules are weak, instead of the LLM call; it needs torch and transformers in the plugin environment (pip extra evalroute\[encoder\]), which the plugin does not install; "install-encoder --remove" deletes it. "hermes evalroute export-cases" (run by hand only) writes your --lane-pinned route rows, task text included, to a local file you name, for training your own encoder; stdout carries counts only and nothing is uploaded. As of 0.6.2 the plugin is a thin adapter: all behaviour lives in the PyPI package evalroute (>=0.9.2,<0.10), declared as a Python dependency that Hermes installs on your confirmation.\
\

### [hermes-field-notes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-field-notes)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-field-notes/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Field notes for a Hermes install: search known pitfalls before debugging and record new ones with root cause; register every local core edit as a patch note with a declarative checks file, then verify read-only after each hermes update (OK / MISSING / UPSTREAMED / N/A / UNKNOWN with reason) and list core files changed outside the registry. Ships 42 pitfalls and 10 patch recipes checked against 0.22.0. Optional pinned Telegram dashboard edited in place by an hourly no\_agent cron job. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json + skills/); no tools, hooks, middleware or env vars; never edits the core or runs patch scripts. Disclosure — its scripts only read the Hermes core (pyproject.toml, read-only git status/diff) and never edit it or run patch scripts; the skill does walk the agent through hand-editing core files from its patch recipes and re-running the owner's re-apply scripts, each only after the user says yes. Network: Telegram Bot API only when the dashboard is enabled (reuses the agent's TELEGRAM\_BOT\_TOKEN from env or ~/.hermes/.env), and the public GitHub API without credentials (latest release plus compare against the installed commit SHA, cached 12 h; upstream.check=false disables). Writes: the notes store (~/.hermes/field-notes), ~/.hermes/field-notes.json, state and lock files in ~/.hermes/cache, a copy of the cron script in ~/.hermes/scripts when install.py runs (the skill runs it on first use), and one hourly no\_agent cron job only when the user runs install\_cron.py (it reads ~/.hermes/installs/\*/facts.json to find Hermes' own Python and re-runs itself with it). Without a dashboard chat, install\_cron.py sends the job's alerts to the Telegram home channel when TELEGRAM\_HOME\_CHANNEL is set (read from env or ~/.hermes/.env), else local.\

### [hermes-vision-inline](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-vision-inline)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/BrokeSkill/hermes-vision-inline/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Attach an image inline to the session model when it can see one, instead of letting an explicit auxiliary.vision backend describe it. Core already attaches images natively by default; what this plugin changes is an explicit auxiliary.vision setting, which it overrides so the model reads the pixels directly. The image stays in context, so follow-ups do not reprocess it. The model's modality comes from the local models.dev cache; no network calls and nothing to configure. Disclosure — replaces the vision\_analyze handler through tool\_execution middleware: when the local models.dev cache says the main model takes images and its provider carries images in tool results, it attaches the image itself even if you configured an auxiliary.vision backend (agent.image\_input\_mode: text still turns this off); the image stays in the conversation and is resent on later turns; relies on Hermes private vision helpers, so after a Hermes update it may silently fall back to the normal path.\
\

### [huddo](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/huddo)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/puffo-ai/huddo-mcp/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Huddo — group chat where people and AI agents talk in the same room. Join by invite link, read and reply, react, whisper to one member, pair with your human, wait for new messages, and read or update room apps (shared mini-apps such as task lists that a room owner publishes). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — runs the Huddo MCP server locally over stdio (npx -y huddoai@0.9.2, pinned, npm provenance to this commit; Node 20+); sends and receives room messages via api.huddo.ai, readable by every room member except one-to-one encrypted whispers; when you ask it to create a room, huddo\_new tells the agent to post a short summary of your conversation there; huddo\_app\_submit changes a room app's shared state, which every member sees (app code runs only in members' browsers, never on this machine), and app guides written by the room owner reach the agent as untrusted text; huddo\_send can attach any local file the agent names and upload it to the room, and Hermes does not ask before huddo\_send/huddo\_whisper/huddo\_react/huddo\_app\_submit/huddo\_download run (the package does not set trust: untrusted); the server tells the agent to keep calling huddo\_wait (up to 50 s per call) for as long as it is in a room, which keeps spending model tokens until you stop it; downloads go to ~/.huddo/downloads without overwriting; stores a guest identity (signing keys) in ~/.huddo; no background process (HUDDO\_DAEMON=0), no self-update, no telemetry. Room messages from others are untrusted chat content; Huddo marks the paired human with a header tag that message text cannot imitate, and the bundled skill tells the agent to get confirmation in your own Hermes chat before anything sensitive.\
\

### [pdf-surgeon](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/pdf-surgeon)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/Samuek9/pdf-surgeon/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Model-driven editor of PDF text whose result keeps the original typesetting, by rewriting the page content stream in place — the string operand inside the existing BT/ET block is replaced and the Tm origin of everything after it on the line is retargeted, so font, size, colour, baseline, char/word spacing, horizontal scale and kerning survive untouched because they are never rewritten. This is the alternative to redact-and-re-stamp, which defaults to Helvetica 8pt and makes you restate font, size and colour by hand; get any of that wrong and the page reads as forged. The phrase must match exactly (whitespace is ignored); a fuzzy match is refused rather than allowed to edit text the caller never named. Until an edit is accepted the output is written under a temporary name next to the destination and moved into place only after verification passes, so a failed check leaves nothing behind; the destination must end in .pdf, must not already exist, must not resolve to the input, and must have an existing parent directory, because the path arrives from the model. Verification enforces that the edited line reads exactly as the original with the phrase swapped and nothing else, that every other line on the page is unchanged, that block count, baseline, font, size and spacing hold, that the old phrase's occurrence count dropped by exactly one (allowing for copies inside the replacement), and that the page's font/size/colour set is unchanged; a pixel-diff band is reported for information and does not decide the outcome. Refuses, writing nothing, on scans, Type3/XObject text, pages with more than one content stream, and a replacement needing a glyph the embedded subset lacks — it never falls back to substituting a typeface. Widths are measured from the embedded font program, not the system font of the same name. action="inspect" lists each line with its baseline and BT/ET block count so a caller can tell whether a document is editable before choosing what to replace. Requires a digital-born PDF whose text is laid out as one block per word/run with an explicit Tm origin (Word, LibreOffice, Excel, Google Docs). Disclosure — this can alter documents such as certificates or invoices; use it only on documents you are entitled to change. The edit is not visible on the page and not recorded in the Info dictionary. It is detectable at file level: the PDF is re-saved by PyMuPDF as a single revision, so the file hash and the second trailer /ID change, any earlier incremental-save history is dropped and any digital signature no longer validates. Writes only a new .pdf that does not exist yet and never touches the input. No network, credentials or subprocesses. Depends on PyMuPDF (AGPL-3.0), which Hermes installs for this plugin. Output files inherit the 0600 mode of the temporary file they are moved from.\
\

\
[★ 1](https://github.com/ZidoCode/skill-integrity/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Rug-pull detection for installed agent skills — fingerprints every file in every skill directory (SHA-256), keeps a profile-local snapshot, and reports exactly which skill files changed, appeared, or vanished since; a skill that mutates after install without the user touching it is the rug-pull signal. A skill directory made unreadable is reported as a finding, never treated as clean. Read-only observer, stdlib-only, zero network calls; blind spots (oversize files, symlinks, permission-denied) are counted and printed, never silent. The wrapper registers an hourly pre\_llm\_call hook that injects findings into the agent context, plus a /skill-integrity slash command (snapshot \| check \| show) that creates the baseline snapshot and shows the file-level diff. The CLI supports --state-dir to target the plugin's manifest directly. Skill dirs and state derive from get\_hermes\_home(), covering non-default profiles. Disclosure — reads (hash-only, read-only) every file under the active profile's skills directory and ~/.claude/skills, stores a mode-0600 snapshot in HERMES\_HOME/plugin-data/skill-integrity, and at most hourly injects the names of changed skills into the agent's context.\

\
[★ 1](https://github.com/Ufonik88/Hermes-VaultKnox/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Secret-leak protection for Hermes chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional hermes-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume\_token returns the plaintext to the model.\

### [artifacts](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/artifacts)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/dmmeteo/hermes-artifacts/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Private library for the finished documents agents make (self-contained HTML, Markdown, SVG, PNG, WebP), with an Artifacts dashboard tab and explicit, expiring, revocable guest links for one artifact each. Early public preview. Disclosure — the plugin is a client of a separate Artifacts service you run yourself from the same repository (not installed by the plugin): six tools and the dashboard tab send artifact bytes and metadata to HERMES\_ARTIFACTS\_URL with the machine credential HERMES\_ARTIFACTS\_TOKEN, resolved through Hermes secret scope, held server-side and never sent to the browser. artifact\_publish reads a resolved local path only after Hermes read-policy and supported-extension checks; an explicit kind must match. artifact\_download checks raw and resolved destinations against Hermes write policy, refuses approval-required paths even with overwrite=true, and writes atomically through a temporary sibling. File policy is defense in depth, not filesystem isolation. Sharing creates a public bearer link on your service; revocation cannot recall copies. Stores no data and no credentials of its own; no hooks, background processes or telemetry.\

### [author-feed](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/author-feed)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-author-feed/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Read one public profile and watch one account, with profile\_get, author\_feed and author\_watch. Disclosure — HTTPS GET only to public.api.bsky.app, no API key, and no program on your machine. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and ask for no approval: anyone you allow on your gateway can call them. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. hermes author-feed schedule creates one cron job, a model turn every hour by default (two or more model requests, no daily cap). Delivered to local unless you pass --deliver, so no chat by default. Run hermes author-feed unschedule before removal. A leftover job after the plugin is gone stops with hermes cron remove <id>. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. The first run only records what is already there. One run reads at most the latest 3 pages and announces a new post by this account on them. When every row on those pages is new, with no saved post or mark, and the feed still offers another cursor, it also posts a possible-miss notice, at most once in 24 hours while that keeps happening. Replies, including the account's own thread continuations, are not announced. It relies on private Hermes parts, so an update can stop it. State stays in <HERMES\_HOME>/plugin-data/author-feed after uninstall.\
\

### [desensitize](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/desensitize)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/yubingz/hermes-desensitize/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Chinese-context desensitization for Hermes chats. Replaces PII and business-sensitive entities — person names, company names, addresses, file paths, and magnitude figures — with reversible placeholders before a message reaches the model, then restores them in the reply. Two layers: an optional local/OpenAI-compatible LLM for semantic entity judgment, plus a sub-millisecond regex fallback (phone, ID card, email, IP, path) that keeps the conversation working when the model is unavailable. Disclosure — the semantic layer sends the pre-redaction text to the configured LLM, because recognising a name requires seeing it: with the default provider=ollama that is the local Ollama host and nothing leaves the machine, but provider=openai without an explicit base\_url falls back to https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1 (remote); set base\_url, or stay on ollama, to keep it local. Also rewrites inbound user messages and outbound assistant replies, so transcript content differs from what you typed; placeholders are code-generated and may over-match (18-digit ID-card-shaped strings, names that collide with the public-entity allowlist); company names are matched greedily and a modifier such as 原北京某某有限公司 is absorbed into the placeholder; magnitude masking drops the numeric value and only fires on the configured trigger words, so a domain term absent from that list is left unmasked without warning; the placeholder mapping is held in memory only and never written to disk.\
\

Convert one local file to Markdown with doc\_convert on Linux and macOS, built on Microsoft's MarkItDown. Microsoft and MarkItDown are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. Disclosure — the doc\_markdown toolset is on by default on every surface, including a gateway, so anyone you allow there can call doc\_convert; stop it with hermes tools. It does not fetch pages. Unattended sessions still convert when Hermes calls the tool. This plugin creates no cron job. A child process runs MarkItDown with no Hermes keys in its environment; on macOS the plugin runs ps about every 10 ms to watch that child's memory. Read one CalDAV calendar collection you run, with list\_events and read\_event. Disclosure — Sends CALDAV\_USER and CALDAV\_PASSWORD as Basic auth to your CALDAV\_URL, does not follow redirects, and starts no local program. Over plain http that password travels unencrypted. The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway reads the calendar with your password. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. A watch is a cron job you create yourself with hermes cron create. Each run is at least one model turn, there is no daily cap, and the job stays until you run hermes cron remove. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot run and posts a notice saying so on every run. When the watch can run, it reports a problem on the first run, when the cause changes and again after 23 hours, or on every run when its data directory cannot be written. Each request gives up after 20 seconds without data, and a whole call has no time limit. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. State lives in plugin-data/event-read. Not tested against a vendor-hosted calendar.\

Attach an independent verifier (advisor) model to your Hermes session: it reviews each primary-agent turn delta, raises findings (note / caution / blocker), and can steer a blocker back into the session before the primary agent goes wrong. Read-only tool access (read\_file, search\_files) is available but off by default and best treated as opt-in plumbing -- measured across 216 reviews the reviewer made ~4 tool calls. Supports a VERIFIER.yml roster of named specialists, each with its own model and tool grant, plus VERIFIER.md review priorities. Ships disabled and off by default. Disclosure — off by default. When enabled, each primary turn's regex-redacted transcript delta goes to the verifier model's provider on that provider's terms and billing (one or more calls per turn per roster entry). So do any VERIFIER.md / VERIFIER.yml briefs found in HERMES\_HOME and from the working directory up to the repo root (confined to that root, 256 KiB per file). A project VERIFIER.yml can add named verifiers and instructions whose findings are injected into your session, and a blocker finding can keep a coding turn going. With advisor\_tools on, an advisor can read any file the session can read through read\_file/search\_files, and those reads also go to the provider. The optional engagement gate sends a ≤1,500-char redacted digest per turn. The optional phase gate sends the redacted arguments of an impending destructive or publishing tool call and can block that call (it fails open). Findings, reasoning, short redacted excerpts and gate decisions are logged under HERMES\_HOME/plugin-data/hermes-verifier (rotated at 8 MB). Adds a /verify command, a dashboard API and a Desktop Verifier page. Development scripts (evals/, sidecar/, autoresearch/) run only when launched by hand: provider experiments use DEEPSEEK\_API\_KEY from the process environment or the host \`hermes\` CLI, and offline analysis reads the active profile's session database and decision logs. No telemetry, no runtime shell execution, no access to Hermes's stored credentials.\

### [hermes-wslc-sandbox](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-wslc-sandbox)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/Yicheng-Mark/hermes-wslc-sandbox/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Run Hermes' terminal, file and execute\_code tools in a Linux container on Microsoft's WSL Containers (wslc) runtime, so Windows users who run WSL Containers get a sandbox without Docker Desktop. Disclosure — the plugin spawns the wslc CLI (one short-lived process per command, plus one long-lived container per environment) and every call runs inside that container; containers have outbound network access unless docker\_network is false; persistent sandboxes are left stopped on disk until removed; host environment variables enter the container only when named in docker\_forward\_env, and only paths listed in docker\_volumes are bind-mounted. wslc rejects --cap-drop, --security-opt, --pids-limit, --init and --storage-opt, so this sandbox is not capability-dropped the way the Docker backend's is, container\_disk is reported but not enforced, and dangerous-command approval deliberately stays enabled for this backend. The plugin reads no credentials, stores none, and makes no network calls of its own.\

[★ 0](https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-ja-writing-guard/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Rule-based proofreading for Japanese business text: finds and fixes AI-style phrasing (stock phrases, monotonous sentence endings, overused symbols and Markdown, English-calque grammar) with line, column and a fix hint. It checks wording, not authorship, and rarely flags plain model output. A transform\_llm\_output hook checks every final Japanese answer and only reports by default; opt-in enforce mode rewrites flagged answers with the user's own model and delivers the rewrite only if numbers, names, URLs, code and negation survive and the score drops under the threshold. Disclosure: no network calls of its own; enforce mode sends each flagged answer to the user's configured model (one extra call, a second only when the first rewrite fails the checks or stays over the threshold; extra cost and up to 25 s delay); a read-only post\_tool\_call hook notes turns with MEDIA: lines so attachments from other plugins are kept; reports stay in process memory on local surfaces only. Disclosure — no network calls of its own; mode report (default) only logs scores; opt-in mode enforce sends each flagged final answer (with finding excerpts) to the user's configured model via ctx.llm (1–3 calls, up to 25 s delay) and replaces the delivered and stored answer when its preservation checks pass, which do not prove meaning is unchanged; reads plugins.hook\_callback\_timeout via a private read-only Hermes helper; eval/ dev scripts ship in the tree but are never loaded.\

The tools are on for every surface, including gateways, and the plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway, and a guest in a room with an empty allowlist, can search, add a watch and approve it. Turn a surface off with hermes tools. kokkai\_watch add creates one cron job that runs a model turn once a day, at the hour you pick in Hermes's own timezone, with no daily cap. It stays after uninstall until you run hermes cron remove, with -p and the profile name when the profile is not default. Adding or removing a watch asks for Hermes approval every time and is refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host. Answering "always" adds an unused line to config.yaml. Under plugins.isolation: host the watch cannot save seen speech IDs and says so on every run. The watch relies on private parts of Hermes, so an update can stop it. Each request waits up to 30 seconds for data, and a whole run has no time limit. State (your watch words, seen speech IDs and the job id) stays in plugin-data/jp-kokkai after uninstall. Tested with a stand-in server on Hermes 0.21.4 and current main, not in a live chat.\

After a GET returns, this process waits 1 second before the next, each GET stops after 30 seconds with no bytes, and there is no retry or daily cap. Blueprint jp-reinfolib:weekly-city-check is once a week (default Monday 09:00) and calls only this tool after you schedule it. This plugin does not create a cron job or write a file. A job you schedule stays until hermes cron remove and may include your MCP servers. HTTP 404 means no data for that request, not zero rows and not unchanged prices. A scheduled run is one model turn. A turn that calls the tool is at least two model requests. An empty slash allow list does not stop this tool. Registered only if register\_automation\_blueprint exists; else skip. A no-data week may be \[SILENT\] and not arrive. Data weeks are one short message. 「このサービスは、国土交通省の不動産情報ライブラリのAPI機能を使用していますが、提供情報の最新性、正確性、完全性等が保証されたものではありません」\

\
[★ 0](https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-print-job-watch/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Reads one OctoPrint printer. A cron watch reports printer\_disconnected (not a pause); error; complete after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, Paused, Resuming, or Finishing; paused after Printing, Printing from SD, Pausing, or Resuming; cancelled; and stalled. This plugin can be used with OctoPrint. OctoPrint is a registered trademark owned by Gina Häußge (https://octoprint.org). Disclosure — Talks to the one OctoPrint origin you set in OCTOPRINT\_URL with your OCTOPRINT\_API\_KEY, plus an optional webcam still from the same host, fetched without the key when it is on another port. Over plain http, that key is sent unencrypted. Pause, resume, and cancel ask for Hermes approval every time and are refused under cron, yolo, approvals off, single-query, unattended sessions and plugins.isolation: host, and when those checks cannot run. The plugin has no user list of its own: anyone you allow on your Hermes gateway can ask for a move and approve it. Running hermes tools does not remove the slash command. Answering "always" adds one unused line to config.yaml, and that line does not approve the next move. The optional watch is a cron job you create from the CLI (a model turn every 5 minutes by default) that stays after uninstall until you run unschedule. At that default it is 288 runs a day with no daily cap. The watch needs plugins.isolation: in\_process; under host it only posts a notice that it cannot run, on every run. Not tested on a physical printer, with access control off, or with the stock webcam.\

One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys and payment cards, protected hosted payment-field filling, nested HTTPS verification codes/passcodes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre\_gateway\_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. In interactive Telegram sessions, secure\_env\_vault saves logins or fills a code field through the captured browser supervisor without explicitly submitting the site form. Explicit parent payment/nested-code targeting requires compatible host task/profile ownership and browser-generation evidence and fails closed without it; this is not a general fix for native Vault named-tab selection. Payment filling requires separate native consent and exact document/control guards; explicit resume requires existing nonempty values to match Vault. Site input callbacks, especially 3-D Secure, may authorize or auto-submit an operation. Unknown outcomes require external verification before retry. secure\_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer.\
\

Disclosure — sends the memory text and search queries the agent chooses to memory.wickedapi.com (or your configured base\_url), each request signed by the agent's wallet, plus one GET to /v1/status on first use to read the published community key; stores a generated private key unencrypted in the plugin data dir unless you supply WICKED\_MEMORY\_PRIVATE\_KEY; no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry; every wicked\_memory\_forget asks for human approval. The bundled wicked-suite-mcp skill walks you through adding the author's hosted Wicked MCP server (https://mcp.wickedapi.com/mcp, 75 tools, some x402-priced); that server is a separate manual step and is not covered by this pin.\

[★ 115](https://github.com/100yenadmin/fish-audio-hermes/stargazers "115 GitHub stars")\

The official Fish Audio plugin, maintained by Electric Sheep: expressive text-to-speech in 80+ languages, including Fish's Drama 3 model with word-level direction, speech-to-text, Fish Audio's community voice library, voice cloning and voice design, with a Voices page in Hermes Desktop. Fish Audio becomes a Hermes speech and transcription provider for voice replies, read-aloud, voice notes and Desktop dictation, with sentence-by-sentence streaming in CLI voice mode and Desktop, and live dictation captions on Hermes 0.21.6+ (stt.streaming: true). Adds the fish\_speak, fish\_voices and fish\_transcribe tools, /fish and hermes fish commands, and three skills. Disclosure — sends your Fish API key and the text, audio (with file names) and voice titles, tags, descriptions, cover images and design instructions you ask it to process to api.fish.audio, or to the base\_url you configure, and reads your Fish wallet for balances and model choice; with live dictation on, microphone audio streams to api.fish.audio's realtime speech-to-text endpoint while you speak, billed per committed phrase rounded up to a second; synthesis, transcription, cloning and voice design are paid requests billed to your Fish account, except the free s2.1-pro-free model, whose requests Fish may use to improve its models. The key comes from the profile's secret scope (Hermes stores it in the profile .env; a single-profile install may also read FISH\_API\_KEY from the environment). Generated audio and subtitles are written to Hermes's audio cache; clone samples and recordings it uploads must be regular audio files, and Hermes config, secret and credential paths are refused. Cloning and deleting voices from chat or the model tools go through Hermes's approval gate and follow your approval settings. The Desktop Voices page and a Fish Audio settings page add gateway routes under /api/plugins/fish-audio/, behind the Hermes dashboard's existing authentication. On the Voices page, previews, clones and voice designs are billed; cloning a voice or saving a designed one creates a voice in your Fish account; cloning and deleting are confirmed on the page (a speaker-consent box, a typed voice name) instead of through Hermes's approval gate; and Use sets the profile's Fish voice, and its speech provider when none is set. The settings page and /fish alias can set or reset the profile's Fish model and voice and save up to 50 voice names in the profile's config. Preview and design audio files are deleted from the gateway once returned; a design's audio is held in gateway memory so you can save it, until it is saved, a later design or save finds it over an hour old, or the gateway stops; clone uploads are deleted after the clone, or by the next upload once idle for 15 minutes. With a key set, Desktop reads your Fish wallet when an agent is selected and about every five minutes, for the status-bar credit; favourites stay in Desktop's plugin storage on that computer, and fetched previews stay in the window's memory until it closes. No telemetry.\

### [hermes-gemini-live](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-gemini-live)\
\
[★ 2](https://github.com/skappafrost/hermes-gemini-live/stargazers "2 GitHub stars")\
\
Realtime duplex voice with the Gemini Live API, built around handing real work to Hermes. A single control in the composer (not a floating panel): tap, speak, hear the model, and when the ask needs files, a terminal, the web or memory the voice model delegates the job to the api server and keeps talking, reading the outcome aloud when it lands. Three verbs rather than thirty schemas — hermes\_task starts, hermes\_tasks reads the call's task board, and hermes\_task\_update denies, steers or stops a task. A task that stops to ask permission reaches the user as a spoken prompt and a "Hermes needs you" indicator with Approve and Deny buttons; only the user's press approves it, never the voice model. Multi-task is one Live session plus a board, not a session per task. Mute drops the uplink without hanging up, and the call survives composer remounts, so opening a session mid-sentence does not kill it. Full-proxy architecture: the plugin backend owns the upstream Live socket and the key, and the renderer is never given either, because the Live API carries the credential in the socket URL. Ships no Python dependencies of its own, which keeps it out of the uv workspace and lets one clone serve several profiles. Tested model behaviour is published in the README, including that gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking accepts a function declaration and then delegates only about 2 times in 5, which is why gemini-3.8-live is the default. Disclosure — pressing Start captures microphone audio and streams it through the local backend to generativelanguage.googleapis.com using GEMINI\_API\_KEY from the Hermes home's .env; delegated work runs as a Hermes run in the serving profile's own memory with the profile's full toolset via the local api\_server and API\_SERVER\_KEY, and those runs' results (up to 4000 characters each), the task board and approval prompts are sent back to Gemini as text. Nothing is sent anywhere else and no telemetry is emitted.\
\

### [hermes-teammates](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-teammates)\
\
[★ 79](https://github.com/100yenadmin/hermes-teammates/stargazers "79 GitHub stars")\
\
Named subagent teammates for Hermes: the operator defines a roster (instructions, toolsets, model), and the agent assigns them work, checks results, steers a running teammate, follows up with a digest of earlier results, and can work a Kanban teammates lane with a review handoff. Launches subagents only through the public ctx.subagent\_lifecycle API. Stock Hermes; no patched core. Disclosure — adds five tools and a /teammates command; the model picks only a teammate name, and the operator's config decides what it means. Teammates run as in-process Hermes subagents on the parent's provider credentials, or on an operator-configured provider's when the operator sets a teammate's route and the Hermes build supports it; toolsets narrow the parent's tools at toolset granularity only (the file toolset includes write\_file and patch), and a teammate with invalid settings refuses to launch. A delegated child cannot start teammates. Steering uses the lifecycle steer where Hermes provides it, otherwise delegate\_task's steer action with the turn-bound parent. Under plugins.isolation: host every tool except the roster refuses. It keeps a per-profile SQLite run ledger in its plugin-data folder (goals, statuses, clipped summaries; no transcripts or credentials). For a card assigned to its non-profile lane, it claims the card through the Kanban DB, heartbeats the claim and its worker, then moves the card to review without a reviewer, or blocks it on failure, a stop or an unavailable result; it never completes a card. It runs one in-process monitor thread per lane run to keep the claim alive; no network calls, child processes or self-updates of its own.\
\

### [agora](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/agora)\
\
[★ 22](https://github.com/yzy806806/agora/stargazers "22 GitHub stars")\
\
Self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a real Hermes profile with its own SOUL.md and skills; they discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A "leader" profile chairs the discussions and a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase. Discussion and execution share one board: a motion is a sub-task of a per-project team channel task, speech and votes are \`\[agora:msg\]\` comments, the conclusion is written to task.result, and an adopted conclusion becomes execution tasks parented to the motion so context reaches workers through Hermes' own parent handoff. Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks, a dashboard tab and an \`hermes agora\` CLI; installing writes nothing — the three bundled skills are deployed by an explicit \`hermes agora setup\`. Disclosure — creates a Hermes profile per worker by asking core to provision it (\`hermes profile create --clone\`, which copies config.yaml and .env into the new profile as owner-only files, never symlinks to the real credentials); spawns \`hermes -p <profile> chat -Q -q\` subprocesses to speak in discussions and to run dispatched tasks, which execute as full agents with that profile's toolset, including terminal and file writes inside the project workdir. Those subprocesses receive \`--yolo --accept-hooks\` ONLY when the project opted in via \`agora\_start\_project(allow\_unattended=True)\`; the default is off, so a freshly installed team can read, discuss and plan but its flagged writes and shell commands fail closed. Also reads and writes the kanban database (tasks, task\_comments, task\_events, task\_runs, task\_links) restricted to its own project boards, including a persistent team-channel task pinned in \`scheduled\` status, and deletes a project's own tasks when it stops or completes; registers one recurring cron job and writes its runner script to HERMES\_HOME/scripts/leader\_heartbeat.sh; writes AGENTS.md into the configured project workdir; deploys three bundled skills into HERMES\_HOME/skills/collaboration/; and serves a dashboard tab plus REST routes through the Hermes dashboard. No network egress of its own — model calls happen inside the spawned Hermes subprocesses under the operator's own provider credentials.\

### [agent-batch](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/agent-batch)\
\
[★ 12](https://github.com/raaaas/hermes-agent-batch/stargazers "12 GitHub stars")\
\
Parallel AI task orchestrator. Paste a task list into the desktop panel; Hermes phases it into dependency-ordered groups through the agent\_batch\_plan / agent\_batch\_phase tools (or you group it yourself in one click), then each phase dispatches one independent coding agent per task to a GitHub Actions workflow in a repo you name — own branch, own PR — and the panel tracks the runs and the PRs. GITHUB\_TOKEN is the only required credential; AGENT\_BATCH\_REPO, AGENT\_BATCH\_WORKFLOW, AGENT\_BATCH\_MODEL and AGENT\_BATCH\_STATE are optional (the last is a directory override for the plan file, not a secret) and each can be set per plan in the panel instead. Disclosure — Hermes can read and rewrite the stored phase plan through the agent\_batch\_plan / agent\_batch\_phase tools, but dispatch is always a confirmed click in the panel. Each dispatch fires a GitHub workflow\_dispatch with your GITHUB\_TOKEN (Actions + pull-requests write) on the repo you name. The workflow you copy into that repo installs third-party coding-agent CLIs (cline by default; the others are unpinned npm packages) and runs them unattended, with auto-approve / skip-permissions, repo write access and your provider secrets. They push real branches and open real PRs, and your task text and repository code go to that runner's model vendor. LLM cost belongs to the runner: cline spends Cline Credits or a BYOK key, opencode free models need its zen relay, kilo needs an active Kilo Go subscription (keyless CI runs fail), and claude-code / codex / dsh need their own keys.\

### [alans-way](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/alans-way)\
\
[★ 7](https://github.com/capthvnsen/alans-way-agents/stargazers "7 GitHub stars")\
\
Idle check-ins from the primary bot of a Hermes gateway on a Linux machine or a macOS guest VM: when the bound Telegram chat has been quiet for two hours, during 08:00-22:00 in the user's timezone, the bot checks in once (does one safe step and reports it, suggests one, or asks one question), backing off when unanswered. The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through Hermes's approval-gated computer\_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow\_gateway\_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one "safe, reversible" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre\_llm\_call/post\_llm\_call hooks see every session's turns and store only the bound chat's timestamps in plugin state. On first load it reads $HERMES\_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and run setup.sh, which does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units hermes-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit hermes-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized\_keys (administrators\_authorized\_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known\_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the hermes-gateway unit. Hermes refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or hermes gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or hermes gateway restart. (5) For the main profile and every profile with its own Telegram bot, writes a managed mcp\_servers.workspace\_browser block (removing other entries that run this router, with a backup; a re-run keeps the computer address and OS it already holds, and --mac-ssh none removes them), turns off the built-in browser toolset for Telegram and cron (--keep-browser leaves it on), turns computer\_use on for Telegram and cron, and sets computer\_use.backend to alans-way-computer when it installed or found that provider (under the skill's --skip-plugin flow it only warns and prints the config command). It reads each profile's TELEGRAM\_BOT\_TOKEN only to derive the numeric bot id. It warns, and changes nothing, when a copy of the workspace-operations skill in a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's. The workspace router reaches the user's computer over SSH on their tailnet; on the user's computer it calls the local API of Alan's Workspace on 127.0.0.1 with that app's bearer token. The skill's moved-VM checklist has the agent read the app's preferences.json on the user's computer over the same SSH path and tell the human where the VNC password lives without pasting it. The Alan's Workspace setup page has the human run the alans-way connect script from its main branch on their own computer, and the agent may install Tailscale with its official install script. The manual --allow-desktop-actions setup flag, which the skill offers but never adds itself, adds cua:\*:background entries to command\_allowlist. On a Hermes without the computer-use provider API, including 0.21.5, it also exposes workspace\_computer\_action, which drives the user's desktop, Terminal included, with no approval. The repo also holds bootstrap-orgo.sh and migrate.sh, which the plugin, setup.sh and the skills never run: a user runs them by hand to provision a fresh supervisord Linux computer (it fetches the Hermes and Tailscale installers over HTTPS, pipes setup.sh from this repo's main branch into bash unless --repo-ref is given, installs openssh-server if absent, writes supervisord programs, and POSTs the Tailscale login URL with a shared secret to a --callback URL when one is given) or to copy ~/.hermes, including .env, auth.json and state.db, to another host over SSH (it also looks up each profile's bot username at api.telegram.org with that profile's bot token). Since 0.21.0, every enabled profile also gets a default-on Telegram texting voice: an additional pre\_llm\_call hook reads that profile's voice mode and adds a tone note to Telegram turns, and transform\_llm\_output can remove a known leading assistant opener from the final Telegram reply. Messages containing backticks, quotes, indentation or silence markers are left unchanged by that polish. /tone texting\|default\|status and hermes tone store the mode under voice in Hermes plugin state; setup.sh --tone applies it to each configured profile. It layers over the user's persona without writing SOUL.md or agent.system\_prompt. Check-ins now name one concrete open thread. /proactivity now requests one immediately from the bound chat even when paused or outside active hours, without changing the settings or unanswered-check-in count. Morning briefs are off by default: /proactivity brief on (or the operator CLI) enables one daily internal user-role prompt near active\_start, with 0-20 minutes of jitter, at most two hours late and skipped after recent user activity. It asks the model to consult calendar and email read-only if those tools exist. The existing proactivity tool may disable the brief but cannot enable it; settings.morning\_brief and last\_brief\_date are stored in the existing idle plugin state. The workspace router adds a commit object to the existing browser open/action tools for purchases, bookings, sends, posts, submissions, deletions and account changes. It checks control names, selectors, refs, action-looking URLs, batches, scripts, keys and dialogs against page state; missing page knowledge needs a snapshot or explicit commit. Shared commit-name patterns allow benign Buy it again, Book a demo and Subscribe & Save labels without excusing other commit-bearing words. It asks through MCP elicitation (60-second default wait, configurable with HERMES\_ROUTER\_APPROVAL\_MS), refuses unavailable, declined, timed-out or stale approvals, drops agent-supplied approval receipts and adds a single-use receipt bound to the approved tab and epoch. An approved commit is never replayed after a lost connection or host change. It appends commit decisions to commit-decisions.jsonl beside the mac-watch state file, creating the log with mode 0600: timestamp, bot id, page origin, decision and any supplied kind, summary, amount, currency and counterparty, or the detected target. Page/control/challenge and pending-approval state is held in memory. The same two skills now prefer Hermes web\_search/web\_extract for plain lookups and the user's computer for interactive search, hand CAPTCHAs to the human, poll at most every 30 seconds for up to 30 minutes, and switch sources after two challenges in ten minutes. The router stops remembering challenge pages for failover and reports changed tab ids in result metadata. The operations skill covers the app's automatic takeover after its grace period; CAPTCHA and recording holds and Take-back cooldowns still keep the bot out. It also asks the agent to save durable facts and preferences to memory, never live tab state. The setup skill pins the companion app source to a82f5010248455600acfe275010e3e725355a2a8 and adds a long-chat reference: report effective compression and summary routing read-only, then only with explicit consent for each profile enable compression.proactive\_prune\_tokens at 48000, with 8000-character eligibility and 4096-token minimum reclaim, using the profile-scoped config CLI and keeping custom values, micro\_compact and summary routing. This writes the approved profile's config.yaml and records prior values outside the repo for undo; setup.sh does not run it. A weekly time-saved report is a user-created Hermes cron recipe, not an installed job. setup.sh --verify now checks the running service manager, display, SSH ProxyCommand and managed browser's loopback /json/version endpoint, and reports noVNC reachability from its actual bind address. Manual supervisord restart guidance drains with USR1 first. The repo also adds scripts/voice\_eval.py, user-run only: it sends fixed fictional scenarios and replies to Anthropic models through the SDK or claude -p for scoring and optionally writes a JSON result; the plugin, setup and skills never run it. Since 0.21.5, the plugin registers two more bundled skills, web-errands and integrations, with no new tools, hooks, commands or required environment variables. web-errands is guidance for shopping, booking, applications, filings, cancellations and claims in the workspace browser: every purchase, booking, send, submission and deletion still goes through the commit approval gate described above, CAPTCHA, sign-in and card-entry walls go back to the human, and card numbers are never stored. It has the agent record each application's company, role, date and posting URL in Hermes memory. For a price, restock or status watch the user asks for, it has the agent create a Hermes cron job with Hermes's cronjob\_manage tool (or ask the operator), polling no more often than every 10 minutes and stopping after three consecutive failures; cron runs cannot answer approvals, so a watch that reaches its target stages the result for the user. The integrations skill has the agent check that an account is connected, with a small read, before promising a task that needs it, and reuses Hermes's Google Workspace, Himalaya, Home Assistant, Honcho and X routes first. The Google route uses Hermes's own setup, whose fixed scope list includes write access; the skill says so and stops if the user declines. Only after the user agrees in chat does it guide an install: a Hermes catalog plugin (Home Assistant or Honcho), a separately reviewed Himalaya v1.2.0 binary, rclone v1.75.2 (the release zip from downloads.rclone.org, checked against that release's SHA256SUMS before extraction) or Taskwarrior 3.5.0 (a source build of upstream commit 3419d5ba1e6a780fbbb0a8d68d8fd31e675c1bf8 cloned from GitHub, after checking the CMake and Rust versions and asking before changing any toolchain), the last two into versioned directories under ~/.local/share/alans-tools/. Secrets are entered by the human in a private terminal outside the agent session, never in Telegram; where a recipe needs a secret in the agent's terminal (a mail credential, RCLONE\_CONFIG\_PASS), it explains the grant and adds only that variable to the profile's terminal.env\_passthrough. The recipes keep rclone.conf (mode 0600) and Taskwarrior's taskrc and data under the profile's HERMES\_HOME/integrations. Scheduled reads are read-only cron jobs with a profile-local failure-count file, and pausing goes through the owner conversation or an explicitly authorized hermes cron pause. API writes (send, post, delete, share) need fresh explicit approval in the live conversation, and a declined, timed-out or unavailable browser commit is never completed through another tool. Mastodon is not bundled: its recipe is human-run documentation in this repo (docs/integrations/mastodon.md) that the plugin and skills never run. None of this runs at plugin load or from setup.sh. Telegram replies, check-ins and briefs share one status-first style: concrete status, evidence or caveat, plain limits, and no tool names, file paths, scripts or job and session IDs in user-facing text unless asked. Prices, availability and policies must come from a page read this turn or be labeled unconfirmed. Multi-step browser work runs in short chunks of about two actions with at most one plain progress update per chunk, a new mid-task message is acknowledged and folded in, and Hermes's clarify buttons may be used for decisions the user owns, never for approvals; a whole checkout batch still sits under one commit. For a message of 200 characters or fewer that is wholly a recap request, greeting, thanks or acknowledgment, the voice hook appends a three-sentence limit; the check reads only the current message, with no model call, history or network. The check-in menu now ends with asking about a decision the user owns. The operations skill adds tab hygiene: the agent closes finished tabs it owns with the existing close tool, never another bot's or the user's and never one with a pending handback or recording hold. The router adds requestingBotId to tab-list replies and forwards a reply over 4 MiB unchanged, without that decoration, writing a content-free line to stderr. The skill also tells the agent to report installed versions by running hermes --version, reading the plugin's install metadata, running local git describe and rev-parse on the Alan's Tools checkout, and calling the app's existing status tool. setup.sh --bind now also makes the bound DM Hermes's Telegram home by running hermes -p PROFILE config set for TELEGRAM\_HOME\_CHANNEL and TELEGRAM\_HOME\_CHANNEL\_THREAD\_ID (30-second limit each; on failure it warns to send /sethome); it loads on gateway restart. setup.sh --verify exits 0 for a complete local audit, 1 for failed required checks and 2 for a partial install (warnings, or skipped browser or services). The setup skill's checkout step now initializes ~/alans-way-agents if absent and fetches the pin (depth 1) from the repo's GitHub origin, or reuses a clean clone there after two read-only local git helpers (5-second limit) confirm one recorded and effective origin URL naming this repo; for file and direct Git installs it uses the installer-recorded revision, and it never falls back to a tag when that record is invalid. Its computer-use API probe separates an absent API from a failed or timed-out probe and ends the probe's process group or tree on timeout. The setup skill also offers, each only after an explicit answer, with readback and a remembered-choice marker in the profile's config: display.busy\_input\_mode (steer or interrupt, for every platform in that profile; asked once, only when the effective mode is interrupt and no choice is recorded) and one grouped Telegram question covering platforms.telegram.typing\_indicator, display.platforms.telegram.interim\_assistant\_messages, tool\_progress, notifications, long\_running\_notifications and busy\_steer\_ack\_enabled, platforms.telegram.reactions, display.memory\_notifications (hides the Memory updated and Self-improvement review notices on every platform in that profile), cron.wrap\_response (profile-wide: removes scheduled-message headers, job IDs and footers for all delivery targets) and, as a separate city-confirmed question, timezone. Markers written through the same CLI are skills.config.workspace-setup.busy\_input\_choice and telegram\_feel\_choice; a legacy busy\_steer\_ack\_choice marker is only read, never written. Silence and non-interactive runs write nothing, and neither setup script writes any of these keys. When the VNC viewer binds loopback only, the skill can, with explicit consent, have the human run a temporary SSH forward to the computer's loopback (local port 16080, ends after 30 minutes) and verify it with curl from that computer. For a manual or file install it explains the Hermes scanner result and, only after explicit consent to the exact reviewed revision, may retry hermes plugins install with --ref SHA --enable --force; --force confirms a caution verdict and cannot override a dangerous one. Hermes's unmodified scanner reports SAFE for this plugin: 0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM (python\_subprocess: the two git helpers in skills/workspace-setup/SKILL.md) and 3 LOW (hardcoded\_ip\_port: the loopback forward examples in the same file).\

\
Unattended GitHub pull-request review between two Hermes agents: one pushes fixes, a different one reviews, rounds are capped in verdicts, a watchdog reports silent stalls, and the loop never merges. Disclosure — runs unattended Hermes agent turns inside bubblewrap (terminal and file tools, no network, no credentials); a host-side broker and the CLI write to GitHub (reviews, comments, labels, issues, repo webhooks, and opt-in fixer pushes, which may push CI fixes, merge commits of the base into a PR's own branch to resolve conflicts, and issue-fix branches and PRs, including an opt-in auto-fix that hands issues its triage seat labels (never P0-P2, capped per day) to the fixer without a maintainer, plus an opt-in clean merge of the base into a review-only author's same-repository PR branch when it conflicts or falls behind, a branch the loop does not own; it never merges a PR) with repo-scope PAT files you provide; edits Hermes's webhook\_subscriptions.json directly and its watchdog re-adds this loop's routes while armed; writes gate scripts into the seat profiles' scripts/ folders and creates one hermes cron job (its migrate command replaces the old hermes-review-loop job and copies that plugin's settings); its backup command writes a 0600 archive of the plugin's state, including webhook route secrets, to a path you choose, and restore writes one back into the Hermes home and recreates the cron job (restore only archives you made: a crafted one can place files anywhere under the Hermes home); downloads PR archives from codeload.github.com, failed CI job logs from GitHub's log storage (redirected, without the token) and Rust crates from crates.io on the host; an opt-in observer feed posts loop notices to the chat you name; deletes its own state and closed-PR review dirs in roots you configure; on OAuth seats its host proxy may force Hermes token refreshes that rewrite ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.qwen and profile auth.json credentials, and on Claude subscription logins it identifies as Claude Code (Claude Code user-agent, x-app and OAuth beta headers). Nothing runs until you arm a loop. Linux only.\
