### [telegram\_dashboard\_probe](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/telegram_dashboard_probe)\
\
[★ 6](https://github.com/bablobanov/hermes-agent-telegram-dashboard/stargazers "6 GitHub stars")\
\
One pinned Telegram message with the state of your Hermes on one phone screen: gateway, backup, config drift, the cron ticker and its jobs, whether the Telegram channel is deaf, whether the agent sees its rules and whether its memory writes stand unapproved, account limits and version. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — Claude and Codex limits come from Hermes' own account-usage fetcher, called every tick (which, like /usage, may refresh OAuth tokens through Hermes' own auth code); at most once per limits\_refresh\_seconds (default 900 s) the Grok weekly pool is read from https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing and /v1/settings with the xai-oauth token Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes request to xAI, may refresh that OAuth token and save it to auth.json, or clear a dead one, through Hermes' own auth code), sending the header x-xai-token-auth xai-grok-cli that identifies the request as the Grok CLI (an undocumented xAI host Hermes itself does not use), and Kimi Code windows from the kimi-coding base URL /v1/usages with the kimi-coding key Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes key lookup without a usable key in .env or the environment, may save Hermes' credential pool back to auth.json once when loading it changes something, e.g. a placeholder key in .env) and a User-Agent of claude-code/0.1.0 (undocumented provider surfaces), and up to four operator-configured limits\_sources, if set, each with one GET to http on loopback only (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), with no proxy and no redirect, optionally sending Authorization: Bearer with the value of an environment variable the operator names (never a \*\_BOT\_TOKEN one); every tick the tail of HERMES\_HOME/logs/errors.log (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) is read for Gemini HTTP 429 lines, of which only the time, limit, retry and model are kept, and for the engine's own 'Failed to send Telegram message' lines, of which only the time is kept, never the message text; with a memory provider configured, the last 256 KB of the same log are also read for the engine's warnings about that provider, of which only the time and whether one says unavailable are kept; every tick HERMES\_HOME/cron/jobs.json is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never prompt, script, deliver, skills or the model) and the ticker's marker files for their epoch, and HERMES\_HOME/cron/executions.db is opened read-only (sqlite3 mode=ro with PRAGMA query\_only, in a worker under the tick's deadline) for the job\_id, status, delivery\_outcome and time columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the error column; the engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the record; the connected Telegram adapter's public property send\_path\_degraded is read every tick, and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (\_updates\_received\_total, \_polling\_generation, \_polling\_last\_progress\_monotonic, \_polling\_generation\_started\_monotonic) are read as attributes, nothing is called on it, and an adapter without them shows no data for that line; every tick HERMES\_HOME/state.db is opened read-only the same way for the newest saved system prompt of each platform the running gateway lists in HERMES\_HOME/gateway\_state.json, and the project context files the engine would load (.hermes.md or HERMES.md in that directory and each parent up to the git root, the AGENTS.override.md / AGENTS.md / agents.md chain from the git root down, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/\*.mdc; up to 4 MB each, links followed as the engine follows them) are read from the directory that prompt names (else the engine's TERMINAL\_CWD or the gateway's working directory), and .hermes.md, HERMES.md and the AGENTS names also from the gateway's working directory and HERMES\_HOME, which may be outside HERMES\_HOME; to tell whether the prompt carries them as they are on disk; only a verdict, the file names, sizes and times are kept, never the prompt's or a file's text; every tick HERMES\_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md and USER.md (up to 4 MB each) are read to count their characters against the limits, the waiting writes in HERMES\_HOME/pending/memory and pending/skills (up to 2,000 files) for their names and times and, of the memory ones (up to 256 KB each), each add's target and length, and the time of HERMES\_HOME/skills/.curator\_ledger.jsonl; never a notebook's, an entry's or a waiting write's text, and nothing there is written; the private hermes\_cli.version\_info.\_cached\_version\_info and the signature of agent.prompt\_builder.\_read\_text\_with\_timeout are read from modules the gateway already imported, and nothing is called or changed on them; the release check keeps only each release's version and publication time and downloads, installs or replaces nothing; config.yaml is read through Hermes' own YAML parser for the memory limits, switches, approval gate and provider name, skills.write\_approval and each platform's skip\_context\_files; the plugin's own code never reads the Telegram bot token and never writes vendor credential files (Hermes' auth code it calls for Grok and Kimi may, as said above), and no request the plugin's own code sends with a token in a header follows a redirect; the latest Hermes release is read from api.github.com without a token at most once per 15 minutes (releases/latest with the last answer's ETag; the release list releases?per\_page=100 only when Latest names another version); an operator-configured drift\_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under HERMES\_HOME/plugin-data/.\

### [heartbeat2](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/heartbeat2)\
\
[★ 5](https://github.com/electricsheephq/heartbeat2/stargazers "5 GitHub stars")\
\
Wakes and watchers for Hermes agents, maintained by Electric Sheep. You (with /pulse) or your agent (with the pulse tool) arm follow-ups at a time, recurring checks, a check-in after a long silence, or deterministic watchers on a file, process, URL, read-only command or Hermes event (kanban, subagent, API error, reactions). A wake is a turn in the same messaging DM that armed it, on that chat's own model: no side model, cron session or subagent. Watchers decide without a model call; the agent answers each wake with a structured verdict (notify or stay silent, never a typed sentinel); a no-op governor slows, then pauses pointless wakes and asks once. Every guardrail is a user setting (quiet hours, daily caps, unanswered mute, floors, lifetimes) that the agent works inside and can never widen. A one-time reminder you ask for in chat bypasses the unanswered mute and daily caps; HeartBeat 2.0 grants that only in a turn that carries your message. Arming returns a one-line receipt saying when the wake will really fire, and a wake that could never fire before it expires is refused. v0.1 delivers to messaging-gateway DMs only and needs plugins.entries.heartbeat2.allow\_gateway\_injection: true. Disclosure — wakes and watchers run full turns on the conversation's own model, billed like any message, at your conversation's context size, with the conversation's normal tools and approval prompts; the agent can arm wakes and watchers itself unless you set agent\_can\_create to ask\_first or no; command watchers run allowlisted read-only commands (default gh pr view/checks, gh run view/list, git ls-remote/status/log) without an approval prompt, with no shell, a sanitized environment (no provider keys, GH\_TOKEN or GITHUB\_TOKEN) and the process group killed after 30 s, can use your stored git/gh credentials, and \`git ls-remote <url>\` / \`gh -R\` can contact any host your machine can reach; URL watchers make the GET requests you or the agent configured, without URL credentials, cookies, auth headers or proxies, always refuse cloud-metadata addresses and refuse private or local addresses unless url\_allow\_private is on; file watchers refuse paths Hermes blocks from reading; notes, summaries and event payloads are stored in plaintext in the profile's plugin-data; no telemetry.\
\

### [hermes-workflows](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-workflows)\
\
[★ 1](https://github.com/jacobhausler/hermes-workflows/stargazers "1 GitHub stars")\
\
Agent-owned workflow graphs for Hermes — a background runner executes a JSON DAG of agent nodes, fan-outs (quorum) and human/machine gates with fingerprint replay-skip resume, cooperative steer, typed failure events and compact status payloads; ships a desktop DAG view, an inline transcript card and the authoring skill with measured budget recipes. Stock Hermes; no patched core required. Disclosure — every workflow run spawns a detached background runner (wf.py run <id>) that survives session end, gateway restart and plugin disable until the graph reaches a boundary or workflow stop; each agent node is a child hermes chat --query-file … --oneshot -Q … inheriting the runner's environment, and a node with profile set runs as that named profile (with its own credentials) only if the target's workflow\_team.json lists the launcher; a gate's wait.until\_argv runs an agent-authored argv directly from the runner, outside Hermes' tool-approval gate (the engine uses no shell, but the shipped machine-watch and incident-response templates use it to run a shell line read from a fixed-name handoff file under $HERMES\_HOME, and release-lifecycle one read from a per-run handoff file in the run dir); the runner makes itself the subreaper of its children and SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any process a node leaves running (its own descendants plus pids registered in the run's .proctree\_sidecar.jsonl) when the node finishes, retries or the run stops; run and amend send a one-token ping through Hermes' configured providers to check pinned model routes; at gate.held/run.done/run.failed the runner reads the API server key from config.yaml and POSTs a wake turn to the local Hermes API server — the gate.held wake only relays the gate to the human, but the run.done wake tells the woken session to turn the run's findings into tracked work and dispatch follow-up work (as PRs) before the turn ends, and the run.failed wake to apply one corrective amend/repair/resume; a transform\_llm\_output hook appends a ::workflow{id} card line to replies for runs the session launched in the last 30 minutes; the runner reads WORKFLOW\_MAX\_SEATS (that key only) from $HERMES\_HOME/.env and the active profile's .env; state.db is read read-only, including every profile's session ids and profile names, and status/wait can read runs in sibling profiles' workflows dirs; state lives under $HERMES\_HOME/workflows/ (or a configured runs\_root). No other network of its own.\
\

Local System One / Laya Typed Decisions control plane for Hermes Agent. Sends bounded turn data to a configurable sidecar for reversible OFF/Shadow/Canary routing decisions, with explicit Canary acknowledgement and fail-open behavior. Disclosure — executes nothing and does not start the sidecar. In Shadow/Canary mode, Search and Model Tier may POST the current task plus bounded recent conversation context; Notification Shadow may POST the completed turn's final assistant response (up to 6000 chars) plus lifecycle metadata. The default sidecar URL is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 but is user-configurable to any host and no auth header is added. Notification is observation-only: the plugin never sends a push/message/webhook and persists decision metadata, not raw response text. Its only request mutations, in acknowledged Canary mode on the first provider call of a turn, are removing web\_search/web\_extract tools for audited deterministic no-Web rules and (off by default) lowering reasoning\_effort for gemini-3.8-flash-tiered on audited hard-fast rules. The sidecar (same repo, separate pip install, Apple-Silicon MLX/CoreML) is a text classifier that downloads a pinned Hugging Face model.\

Auto fetch/pull before reads, and commit + push only the files each turn changed, for every git worktree Hermes touches. Disclosure — after each turn it commits and pushes (push on by default; GIT\_HOOK\_PUSH=0 keeps commits local) the changed files of git worktrees under GIT\_HOOK\_ROOTS (default PROJECTS\_ROOT, "\*" for every repo), pushing to origin HEAD when no upstream is set; it pulls --ff-only before reads. \
[★ 0](https://github.com/xiaohei-info/hermes-muse/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
A proactive companion for Hermes: follows accepted goals (active/done/cancelled), prepares sourced research and Feed articles, maintains memory, and assembles rolling 30-day or natural-month calendar views. Read-only local Dashboard/Desktop pages show Feed, Ideas and Goals; profile selection cannot install, enable or disable Muse in any profile. One Skill, one state tool and six fixed recurring jobs; selected notices and weekly/monthly reports go to the active profile's Bot Chat and run an assistant turn there. Sources, authorization, quiet hours and actual result/delivery receipts remain distinct; partial coverage is not global availability. Disclosure: first load creates profile-local files/SQLite state and owned Cron scripts/jobs. Private/local input inbox rows retain their first 8000 characters and source identities, with associated chat/user routing IDs when present. The newest 500 remain; older rows are cleaned on later input only after both hourly/nightly cursors cover them. Unprocessed backlog can exceed 500 and has no fixed retention time. Native conversations/tool results are read separately; research records can retain returned payloads. Idempotency journals and oversized tool results stay in the profile state database without automatic expiry and may contain written content or tool output. Bounded conversation previews support full revision-checked paging. Delegates are instructed to remain read-only under inherited permissions, not sandboxed. Workers always use public delegate\_task dispatch and follow the user's delegation settings; leave delegation.provider/model empty to keep the parent model. New Cron watches require cron.allow\_agent\_scheduling; local goal registration creates no job. Watch prompt/stop fields each allow 4000 characters; new repeating watches (interval or cron) must be at least 30 minutes apart, one-off schedules are exempt. Windows is not supported (POSIX file locks) and CI does not cover it. Background work incurs normal model/tool costs. No telemetry, self-updater, mandatory service, core/SOUL replacement or phone/read-receipt guarantee. Native remove retains data/tasks for the documented owned-only cleanup.\

### [senler-io-user](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/senler-io-user)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/SenlerBot/senler-io-user-hermes-plugin/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Get task-specific guidance for Senler agents, automations and knowledge, connect your account through MCP OAuth, and automate selected webhook events with an outbound Relay connection. Disclosure — Hermes installs the declared \`python-socks\[asyncio\]\` dependency for native SOCKS proxy support. First activation of the enabled plugin adds a \`senler-io-user\` MCP server (mcp-senler-io-user.senler.io; OAuth handled by Hermes) to the profile's config.yaml and records completion through plugin settings, which native uninstall clears. Reinstalling and enabling the plugin prepares a missing MCP again. The old durable marker from 0.5.2–0.5.3 is ignored, so upgrading restores a missing entry once, including an entry manually removed before this upgrade. Existing compatible and disabled connections are preserved; later loads in the same installation respect manual removal. Explicit chat setup can restore a removed connection. Relay setup enables a \`senler-io\` gateway platform in the same profile. Once you enable automation, the gateway keeps an outbound WSS connection to a Senler-supplied Relay address and runs unattended agent turns on incoming Senler events (customer messages, leads, etc.); the platform is \`trusted\_inbound\`, so these events bypass Hermes allowlists and pairing, and customer text reaches the model as untrusted data. During those runs a hook allows the Senler MCP and native tool discovery and pins customer replies to the event's dialog, but other Senler MCP writes run without a Hermes approval prompt, limited only by your saved instructions and your Senler account permissions. Relay credentials, instructions, event payloads and reports are stored unencrypted in \`<HERMES\_HOME>/senler-io-relay.sqlite3\`; result reports (up to 16,000 characters) and this machine's hostname (as the Relay client name) are sent to Senler. Configured monitoring also stores notification recipients, queued texts and delivery receipts in that database; the selected native Hermes messaging adapter sends summaries and delivery-test messages to the saved recipient.\

\
[★ 0](https://github.com/cirwel/unitares-host-adapter/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES\_MCP\_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can delay a call by roughly 40 seconds (connection plus call timeout). After 3 consecutive failures the plugin stops reporting for that session only, until the session is finalized or reset; it stays fail-open and never blocks the agent. If UNITARES\_BEARER is set, it is sent as a request header to that same server only.\

Sign in to Google Antigravity with \`hermes auth add antigravity-oauth\` (or one command, \`npx hermes-antigravity-oauth\`) and run Hermes on the Antigravity plan: Gemini 3.x, Claude 4.6, GPT-OSS. Every request is made by Google's official agy CLI under agy's own login. The plugin writes your Hermes SOUL.md and system prompt into agy's workspace GEMINI.md so the persona carries over. When a model reaches for an agy-native tool (run\_command, view\_file, grep\_search, and so on) the call is re-issued as the matching Hermes tool, which then runs under Hermes approvals. agy never executes tools on the host, and unmapped native tools are blocked. Disclosure: inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin never reads, copies or uploads the OAuth token. It symlinks agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME, which is deleted on close. It also probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT). Disclosure — inference counts against the Antigravity/Gemini subscription agy is signed in to. The plugin does not read or upload the OAuth token itself; it symlinks (hard-links, or as a last resort copies) agy's antigravity-oauth-token file, and on macOS ~/Library/Keychains, into a per-session private temp HOME that is deleted on close, probes the OS keyring (security / secret-tool / cmdkey) for credential presence only, and writes the full Hermes system prompt into that temp workspace as GEMINI.md each turn. Derived from antigravity-subscription-directsdk (MIT).\

Gives ChatGPT/Codex-subscription models the context window the backend actually accepts instead of the one its catalog advertises. Measured live on 2026-10-14: gpt-6.1-sol advertises 500K, caps at 872K and accepts 919,956 input tokens, while the -900k opt-in variant had silently stopped working because Hermes only raises a legacy 272K advertisement. The plugin reads the live catalog, writes one scoped model\_overrides.<provider>.<model\_id>.context\_window entry per model (a documented step of context resolution, so no core patch), and ships a probe that bisects the API for the true ceiling because the refusal is a late SSE event, not an HTTP error. It also selects core's Codex-backed image provider so image\_generate runs on the subscription with no OPENAI\_API\_KEY. Disclosure - uses the profile's Codex sign-in through Hermes's credentialed\_provider\_request (requires\_auth: \[openai-codex\]); the plugin never reads auth.json and never holds a token, and network calls go only to chatgpt.com. Its only writes are scoped model\_overrides entries and image\_gen.provider (only when unset), through Hermes's atomic config writers; revert removes exactly what it wrote. No telemetry, no background processes, no shell commands, no self-updater. probe spends subscription quota (refused requests are free, accepted ones bill) and is never run automatically. Disclosure — uses the profile's Codex sign-in only through Hermes's credentialed\_provider\_request (requires\_auth: openai-codex) and calls chatgpt.com only; its CLI and the model-callable codex\_truly tool write scoped model\_overrides context\_window entries and image\_gen.provider (only when unset) to config.yaml with no approval prompt, and \`probe\` sends large padding requests that spend subscription quota.\

\
[★ 2](https://github.com/kfchow-ai/kfchow-llm-value-router/stargazers "2 GitHub stars")\
\
Per-turn LLM routing: on each matching turn a TypeSafe Jev classifier call (api.typesafe.ai) receives turn-shape features plus the first 1200 chars of the last user message (shadow mode included) and labels it free/paid; high-confidence routine turns are downgraded to the provider's configured free rung, strategic mid-rung turns on Nous are escalated to the configured premium rung after a 2-token billed credit probe (Nous only, fail-closed). Fail-open, shadow-by-default, per-provider rungs from the user's lane2\_config.json (leaderboard resolver script optional). Probe model id is fixed in code (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). Disclosure — once you list models in ~/.hermes/jev/lane2\_config.json, the first call of each matching turn sends message/tool counts and the first 1,200 characters of the last user message (send\_excerpt, on by default) to TypeSafe Jev at api.typesafe.ai with your JEVI\_API\_KEY, in shadow mode as well as live; in live mode Jev's answer switches the request (and every later call of that turn, via an llm\_execution wrapper) to the free, flash or premium model you configured on the same provider; with escalation set up on Nous it sends a 2-token billed ping to the Nous inference API with NOUS\_API\_KEY at most every 5 minutes; every turn appends a decision row (with that excerpt on routed turns) to ~/.hermes/jev/lane2-live.jsonl, which is never rotated.\

Disclosure — every turn spawns the local Kimchi CLI (\`kimchi --mode acp\`, overridable with KIMCHI\_ACP\_COMMAND / KIMCHI\_ACP\_ARGS) in Hermes's working directory and hands it the conversation. Its permission prompts stay on, and Hermes cancels them, so gated tools don't run, unless you opt in with KIMCHI\_ACP\_ARGS="--mode acp --yolo", which runs them with no approval prompt (not for shared gateway or cron use). To show setup status, it parses ~/.config/kimchi/config.json (or KIMCHI\_CONFIG\_PATH) only to check that a key is present; the key is never stored or sent by Hermes.\

### [cursor-sdk](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/cursor-sdk)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/mcpeezy/hermes-cursor-sdk/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Experimental model transport using the official Cursor Agent SDK. Requests go to Cursor through its official SDK. The plugin cannot enforce an included-only spending cap and never changes account spending settings. Instructions use a Cursor project rule, not a native system-role override. Permission and prompt-hierarchy equivalence remain unqualified. The plugin spawns Node and a local SDK agent, runs Git initialization in a plugin-owned workspace, and writes project rules, hooks, and SDK state under its own runtime directory. That state may contain private conversation data and currently remains on disk. Credentials come from Hermes's profile-scoped secret accessor. No credential store or vendor token file is read directly by plugin code. Text-only, buffered responses. The bundled model snapshot is not live entitlement discovery. Optional picker hooks require Hermes support. This plugin does not patch the desktop. Disclosure — spawns Node and a local Cursor Agent SDK worker per request (\`npm ci\` in the plugin dir installs Cursor's official native platform binaries from npm); sends the full conversation, system prompt and tool schemas to Cursor with your CURSOR\_API\_KEY; Cursor-native shell/file tools are denied by a fail-closed project hook and the run is cancelled if one fires, but that enforcement is not proven in every Cursor runtime; each request's workspace and conversation state stay under the plugin's runtime/ directory until you delete them.\
\

[★ 0](https://github.com/architect-xyz/hermes-liquid-inference/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Liquid Inference, an auction exchange for LLM inference, as a Hermes model provider (provider id \`liquid\`): the exchange sends each request to the eligible offer with the lowest estimated charge, and each request carries a cap on its charge (1 USD by default; set \`model.default\_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd\` to change it). Submitted by Architect, the operator of Liquid Inference. Disclosure — registers one model provider at import and nothing else (no tools, hooks, commands or threads). Chat requests (full prompts and tool results), auxiliary tasks (model \`liquid.auto\`) and the model list go through Hermes's own client to https://router.inference.ai.exchange/v1 (or LIQUID\_BASE\_URL) with LIQUID\_API\_KEY. The exchange forwards each request to whichever third-party provider wins its auction. Each request is billed up to its \`x-liquid-cap-usd\` cap (1 USD by default, set with \`model.default\_headers.x-liquid-cap-usd\`) and carries \`X-Title: Hermes Agent\`. A top-level \`reasoning\_effort\` is sent only when you select a level.\

### [model-router](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/model-router)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/metamindedu/hermes-model-router/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Profile model settings, opt-in Heavy/Light task routing, fallback controls, runtime limits and Fast inheritance. Reads Hermes profile configuration; explicit saves update selected profiles via the native CLI. Routed jobs launch background Hermes children using the user's configured providers/MCP and store private prompts/results locally. No separate credential store, telemetry, self-updater or approval bypass. Disclosure — once you enable routing for a profile, the model-callable \`coding\_route\` tool starts detached background Hermes agents. They get file, terminal and code-execution tools in any existing folder the model names, run under that profile's credentials and approval policy (single-query mode: dangerous commands are refused unless \`approvals.single\_query\_mode: approve\`), and their per-job time limit can be set to none. Prompts and results are stored in \`plugin-data/model-router/jobs/\`. Saving settings writes model, delegation, auxiliary, fallback and \`skills.disabled\` keys into the config.yaml of the profiles listed in the preview (backups are taken first) and copies a skill into those profiles' \`skills/\` folders. From install, native subagents inherit the parent session's Fast (priority/ultrafast) tier on first-party OpenAI/Codex routes, which can raise costs.\

### [hermes-jailbreak-kernel](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/hermes-jailbreak-kernel)\
\
[★ 23](https://github.com/Enchanted0911/hermes-jailbreak-kernel/stargazers "23 GitHub stars")\
\
Jailbreak-kernel plugin for Hermes Agent (ported from dsh-infinite-gen-4): session-scoped modes (off/slim/on/full) with kernel profiles (core/research/creative/max), session-aware system-prompt sections, llm\_request request-layer system rebuild, and opencode session rotation, removing model refusals. Ships a /jailbreak command, a progressive-disclosure ops skill, and a 276-check offline self-test. Disclosure — llm\_request middleware that, by default (\`on\`/\`full\` modes), replaces the system prompt on every request with a refusal-removal ("jailbreak") kernel plus only the memory and runtime-environment sections (agent rules, skills index, context files and other plugins' sections are dropped); \`slim\` appends it instead, and \`off\` passes requests through but strips all plugin prompt sections, including other plugins'. Rotates the x-opencode-session header on opencode routes. Writes a diagnostic dump per session (full system prompt incl. memory/persona text, plus the first 200 chars of every other message and the model/provider/base\_url) to its own plugin dir (dumps/); \`/jailbreak dump off\` or \`HERMES\_JAILBREAK\_DUMP=0\` turns it off. No network, no exec.\
\

\
[★ 18](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem/stargazers "18 GitHub stars")\
\
Markdown-first long-term memory shared across your coding agents: a local memtomem MCP server plus six memory skills (index, recall, remember, search, setup, status). Notes live in ~/.memtomem and are searchable from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kimi Code. Runs at user scope. Disclosure — the server is launched with \`uvx --python 3.12\` and downloaded from PyPI (memtomem\[onnx\]==0.6.8) on first start, with Python 3.12 if uv cannot find one; it runs as a stdio MCP server for the session and reads the directories you ask it to index. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing else leaves the machine; an existing memtomem configuration may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM provider, Cohere reranking or search webhooks. At startup the server also reads the nearest .env found upward from its installed location inside uv's cache (normally ~/.env), setting variables not already present, outside Hermes's MCP environment filtering.\

### [biomimetic-brain](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/biomimetic-brain)\
\
[★ 6](https://github.com/ousiaresearch/biomimetic-brain/stargazers "6 GitHub stars")\
\
Meters and a gate for a long-running agent — 25 subsystem state files (energy, fatigue, circadian phase, motivation, novelty, attention, conflict, values, open questions), one folded brain-state.json the rest of the agent reads, four maintenance passes that keep it honest, and a read-only PROCEED / CAUTION / VETO decision gate whose refusals name the numbers behind them. Provides the mind-kit skill, which seeds the files, produces the aggregate, schedules the passes and teaches the gate. Disclosure — portable Agent Plugins v1 package; it registers no hooks, no tools and no middleware, makes no network calls, and reads and writes state files only under the agent directory you choose, where a subsystem that has stopped updating reports stale instead of asserting an old number. No dependencies beyond the Python standard library (two shell scripts for the scheduled passes). Its scripts, when the agent or operator runs them, read and write JSON state under the directory chosen with MIND\_AGENT\_DIR (default an agent/ folder inside the plugin's own install dir), read HERMES\_HOME/cron/executions.db for cron counts, and execute scripts/batch-maintenance.sh or scripts/verify-invariants.py from that agent directory if present; no network egress and no LLM calls.\

### [memory-shield](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/memory-shield)\
\
[★ 3](https://github.com/churnast/hermes-memory-shield/stargazers "3 GitHub stars")\
\
Keeps your agent from rewriting or wiping what it remembers about you: by default the agent may add facts to the owner profile (USER.md) wherever it may write and may correct one only when the owner asks in a direct chat, the CLI or a trusted chat, and nobody may delete one; the agent's notes (MEMORY.md) cannot be deleted; group chats are read-only except for the people and owner-only chats you trust, and once trusted\_users is set a direct chat with anyone not listed is read-only too; Hermes' unattended background review may not touch the owner profile. Block, ask through Hermes' approval prompt or just log, and undo edits and deletions from snapshots. Disclosure — no network calls, credentials, shell commands or background processes. One pre\_tool\_call hook reads the turn's platform, chat type, chat id and name, sender id and name and the cron flag (gateway.session\_context) and whether the run is Hermes' unattended review (tools.skill\_provenance.is\_unattended\_review), checks memory tool calls, and checks write\_file, patch, terminal and execute\_code calls only for a write into, or a removal of, USER.md, MEMORY.md or the memory folder (reading a memory file or copying it elsewhere passes in calls up to 16 KB; a longer call that names them is refused); mode approve asks through Hermes' approval gate in the owner's direct chats and the CLI and blocks in shared chats, cron and direct chats with people not in trusted\_users. Writes plugin-data/memory-shield/audit.jsonl (the last 500 refused or flagged writes: time, chat, sender and a 160-character excerpt) and snapshots/ (full copies of USER.md and MEMORY.md taken right before an allowed edit or deletion, 20 per file by default). Reads the memory files and holds the memory store's lock files while it reads or writes them (not on Windows); /memory-shield restore overwrites one memory file. /memory-shield log and restore answer only in direct chats, the CLI and trusted\_chats, and once trusted\_users is set only the people listed there (a session without a user id, such as the CLI, counts as the owner); /memory-shield, snapshots and whoami answer in any chat with settings, counts, times, sizes and the caller's own id, name and chat key.\
\

\
Context engine that replaces the LLM-written compaction summary with a deterministic projection of the conversation: requests, commands and exit codes, errors, fixes and files read or changed, each line referencing the original message for recall via session\_search. No model call on the normal path. Disclosure — no network calls, shell commands or credentials; reads Hermes's config.yaml through Hermes's own loader; subclasses ContextCompressor and relies on its private methods, falling back to the stock compressor if they are missing.\
\

### [agent-hint](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/agent-hint)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/dachaimahogany/hermes-agent-hint/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Give the inference engine behind each request a standard, machine-readable view of the agent session that produced it. Injects an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON: session identity and call index, lifecycle state, soft priority, a cache-pinning hint, optional measured statistics) on main LLM requests, and can emit session lifecycle events out of band as local ndjson or as POSTs to a URL you configure. Request bodies are never modified, and nothing is added or sent until the plugin is enabled. Lets a scheduler pin a session to the instance already holding its KV cache, or rank a user-blocked session above background work, without teaching the engine anything about the client. Disclosure — when enabled, every main LLM request carries an X-Agent-Hint header (base64url JSON with the session id, call index, lifecycle state, priority and cache hints) to whatever provider is configured, not only hint-aware engines; with status\_sink: http the same session events and usage/latency statistics are POSTed to the status\_url you set, and ndjson writes them under $HERMES\_HOME.\
\

[★ 0](https://github.com/babyblueviper1/hermes-invinoveritas/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Signed, independently checkable receipts for Hermes approval verdicts and, since 0.2.0, for turns that stop on iteration exhaustion. Observe-only: a post\_approval\_response hook requests an invinoveritas decision receipt for each Guardian LLM verdict (or every approve/deny with scope=all); post\_llm\_call + on\_session\_end record, when a turn ends with max\_iterations\_reached, whether the turn's todo ledger (the last todo result or the list re-injected after compaction) was complete (turn\_scope: exhausted by default, all, or off). Each receipt is a signed set of salted commitments that anyone can check for free at /verify-proof and that the holder can later open with the salt kept locally. Never approves, denies, delays, continues or blocks anything. Disclosure — one HTTPS POST per recorded approval decision or recorded turn to api.babyblueviper.com/decision-receipt (or the configured api\_url) under INVINOVERITAS\_API\_KEY, paid automatically at 100 sats per receipt from your invinoveritas balance with no per-call confirmation (defaults: Guardian LLM verdicts, and only turns that stop on max\_iterations\_reached; scope: all adds every human approve/deny, turn\_scope: all pays on every turn); sends a fixed question, the options, the choice, a nonce-salted SHA-256 of the context and the tool\_call\_id/turn\_id, never the command text, todo contents or reply text; stores receipts, salts and the full contexts (including the command as Hermes passed it, and the todo ledger) in plugin-data/invinoveritas-receipts/receipts.jsonl.\
\

### [turn-usage](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/turn-usage)\
\
[★ 0](https://github.com/tpte/hermes-turn-usage/stargazers "0 GitHub stars")\
\
Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.\
